#!/bin/bash
# Create temporary GUI desktop LXC for Google Takeout downloads
# Downloads directly to NAS storage via VNC desktop with Chrome

set -e

CONTAINER_ID=600
CONTAINER_NAME="desktop-tmp"
TEMPLATE="local:vztmpl/ubuntu-24.04-standard_24.04-2_amd64.tar.zst"
PROXMOX_HOST="root@homelab"

echo "=== Creating Temporary Desktop LXC ==="
echo ""

# Check if container already exists
if ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct status $CONTAINER_ID" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "Container $CONTAINER_ID already exists."
    echo "Run 'task desktop:destroy' first, or use 'task desktop:info' to get connection details."
    exit 1
fi

echo "[1/6] Creating LXC container (privileged for NAS mount)..."
ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct create $CONTAINER_ID $TEMPLATE \
    --hostname $CONTAINER_NAME \
    --cores 4 \
    --memory 4096 \
    --swap 512 \
    --rootfs nvme-containers:32 \
    --net0 name=eth0,bridge=vmbr0,ip=dhcp,type=veth \
    --features nesting=1,keyctl=1 \
    --unprivileged 0 \
    --onboot 0"

echo "[2/6] Adding NAS mount point..."
ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct set $CONTAINER_ID -mp0 /tank/photo-import,mp=/downloads"

echo "[3/6] Starting container..."
ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct start $CONTAINER_ID"

# Wait for container to get IP
echo "    Waiting for network..."
sleep 10

# Fix DNS (Tailscale DNS may not resolve external hosts)
ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct exec $CONTAINER_ID -- bash -c 'echo nameserver 8.8.8.8 > /etc/resolv.conf'"

# Get container IP
CONTAINER_IP=$(ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct exec $CONTAINER_ID -- ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep inet | awk '{print \$2}' | cut -d/ -f1")
if [ -z "$CONTAINER_IP" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Could not get container IP. Container may still be starting."
    echo "Try: ssh $PROXMOX_HOST 'pct exec $CONTAINER_ID -- ip addr'"
    exit 1
fi
echo "    Container IP: $CONTAINER_IP"

echo "[4/6] Installing XFCE desktop + VNC..."
ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct exec $CONTAINER_ID -- bash -c '
    export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
    apt-get update
    apt-get upgrade -y
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        xfce4 \
        xfce4-terminal \
        dbus-x11 \
        tigervnc-standalone-server \
        tigervnc-common \
        tigervnc-tools \
        wget \
        gnupg \
        ca-certificates
'"

echo "[5/6] Installing Google Chrome..."
ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct exec $CONTAINER_ID -- bash -c '
    wget -q -O - https://dl-ssl.google.com/linux/linux_signing_key.pub | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/google-chrome.gpg
    echo \"deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/google-chrome.gpg] http://dl.google.com/linux/chrome/deb/ stable main\" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/google-chrome.list
    apt-get update
    apt-get install -y google-chrome-stable
'"

echo "[6/6] Configuring VNC server..."
# Generate random VNC password
VNC_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -base64 8 | tr -dc 'a-zA-Z0-9' | head -c 8)

ssh "$PROXMOX_HOST" "pct exec $CONTAINER_ID -- bash -c '
    mkdir -p /root/.vnc

    # Create xstartup script
    cat > /root/.vnc/xstartup << \"EOF\"
#!/bin/bash
unset SESSION_MANAGER
unset DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS
export XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11
exec dbus-launch --exit-with-session startxfce4
EOF
    chmod +x /root/.vnc/xstartup

    # Set VNC password
    echo \"$VNC_PASSWORD\" | vncpasswd -f > /root/.vnc/passwd
    chmod 600 /root/.vnc/passwd

    # Create Chrome desktop shortcut with custom download dir
    mkdir -p /root/Desktop
    cat > /root/Desktop/chrome.desktop << \"EOF\"
[Desktop Entry]
Version=1.0
Type=Application
Name=Google Chrome
Comment=Access the Internet
Exec=/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable --no-sandbox --disable-gpu %U
Icon=google-chrome
Categories=Network;WebBrowser;
EOF
    chmod +x /root/Desktop/chrome.desktop

    # Create readme on desktop
    cat > /root/Desktop/README.txt << \"EOF\"
=== Google Takeout Download Instructions ===

1. Open Chrome (icon on desktop)
2. Go to: https://takeout.google.com
3. Sign in to your Google account
4. Deselect all, then select only \"Google Photos\"
5. Click \"Next step\"
6. Choose: Export once, .zip format, 2GB file size
7. Click \"Create export\"
8. Wait for export to complete (you will receive email)
9. Download all zip files

IMPORTANT: Set Chrome download location to /downloads
- Chrome Settings > Downloads > Location: /downloads

Files will be saved to /downloads which is mounted to:
/tank/photo-import on your NAS

After downloading, process with:
  task photo-import:process
EOF

    # Start VNC server
    vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 -localhost no
'"

echo ""
echo "=== Desktop LXC Created Successfully ==="
echo ""
echo "VNC Connection Details:"
echo "  Host: $CONTAINER_IP:5901"
echo "  Password: $VNC_PASSWORD"
echo ""
echo "On macOS:"
echo "  1. Open Finder"
echo "  2. Press Cmd+K (Connect to Server)"
echo "  3. Enter: vnc://$CONTAINER_IP:5901"
echo "  4. Password: $VNC_PASSWORD"
echo ""
echo "Or use any VNC client (RealVNC, TigerVNC) to connect to:"
echo "  $CONTAINER_IP:5901"
echo ""
echo "After downloading Google Takeout files to /downloads, run:"
echo "  task photo-import:process"
echo ""
echo "When done, cleanup with:"
echo "  task desktop:destroy"

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Usage:
#   1. When deploying a new service, check `local.next_available_ip` for the
#      next free IP in the LXC range (192.168.1.150-199)
#   2. Add the new allocation to the appropriate category below
#   3. Use `local.ip_registry.<category>.<name>` in your module configs
#
# Ranges:
#   - 192.168.1.1-99:     Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches)
#   - 192.168.1.100-149:  Core services (Traefik, Portainer, DNS)
#   - 192.168.1.150-199:  LXC containers (apps)
#   - 192.168.1.200-224:  Reserved for manual/temporary use
#   - 192.168.1.225-254:  Special services & overflow
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    netmask = "/24"
    prefix  = "192.168.1"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - All Static Allocations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure devices (1-99)
    infrastructure = {
      router           = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox          = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host
    }

    # Core services (100-149)
    core = {
      portainer        = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC 100 - Container management
      network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Unbound
      traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
    }

    # Application LXCs (150-199 preferred range for new deployments)
    apps = {
      dashboards       = "192.168.1.234"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia         = "192.168.1.225"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
      immich_importer  = "192.168.1.159"  # LXC 303 - Photo import (estimated)
      immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
      jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "192.168.1.227"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack (Radarr, Sonarr, etc)
      monitoring       = "192.168.1.229"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui        = "192.168.1.221"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n              = "192.168.1.213"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }

    # Reserved IPs (for future use or manual assignment)
    reserved = {
      # 192.168.1.200-224 - Manual/temporary use
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for collision detection
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_allocated_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.infrastructure),
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.apps),
  )

  # Extract the last octet from each IP for range calculations
  _allocated_octets = [
    for ip in local._all_allocated_ips : tonumber(split(".", ip)[3])
  ]

# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration

    gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    netmask = "/24"
    prefix  = "192.168.1"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - All Static Allocations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_registry = {

    apps = {

      immich_importer  = "192.168.1.159"  # LXC 303 - Photo import (estimated)
      immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
      jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "192.168.1.227"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack (Radarr, Sonarr, etc)
      monitoring       = "192.168.1.229"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui        = "192.168.1.221"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n              = "192.168.1.213"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }

    # Reserved IPs (for future use or manual assignment)
    reserved = {
      # 192.168.1.200-224 - Manual/temporary use
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for collision detection
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_allocated_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.infrastructure),
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.apps),
  )

  # Extract the last octet from each IP for range calculations
  _allocated_octets = [
    for ip in local._all_allocated_ips : tonumber(split(".", ip)[3])
  ]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Next Available IP Calculator
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Scans the preferred LXC range (150-199) for the next free IP.
  # Falls back to extended range (200-224) if primary is full.

  # Primary range: 150-199 (50 IPs for LXC apps)
  _primary_range = [for i in range(150, 200) : i]

  # Secondary range: 200-212 (for overflow, avoiding special services at 213+)
  _secondary_range = [for i in range(200, 213) : i]

  # Find first available in primary range
  _available_primary = [
    for octet in local._primary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # Find first available in secondary range
  _available_secondary = [
    for octet in local._secondary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)

  # The next available IP (primary range first, then secondary)
  next_available_ip = length(local._available_primary) > 0 ? (
    "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_primary[0]}"
  ) : (
    length(local._available_secondary) > 0 ? (

    ) : "NO_IPS_AVAILABLE"

  ip_cidr = {

# Homelab Infrastructure

OpenTofu-managed homelab on Proxmox. All commands run from local machine.

## Quick Reference

```bash
# OpenTofu workflow
task tofu:init APP=dashboards
task tofu:plan APP=dashboards
task tofu:apply APP=dashboards

# Utility commands
task tofu:ssh APP=dashboards           # SSH to LXC
task tofu:sync:compose APP=dashboards  # Sync compose files
task tofu:logs APP=dashboards SERVICE=homepage

# Desktop LXC (temporary GUI for downloads)
task desktop:create
task desktop:info
task desktop:destroy

# Backup operations
task backup:status                 # View backup status
task backup:now APP=immich         # Manual backup
task backup:all                    # Backup all containers
task backup:list APP=immich        # List backups
task backup:restore BACKUP=file TARGET_ID=305
task backup:immich:db              # Dump Immich database

# IP address management
task ip:next                       # Get next available IP for new LXC
task ip:list                       # Show all allocated IPs
```

## Architecture

- **Proxmox Host**: 192.168.1.215 (SSH: `ssh root@homelab`)
- **Traefik LXC**: 192.168.1.162 (ID: 200)
- **Monitoring LXC**: 192.168.1.229 (ID: 500)
- **IaC**: OpenTofu with bpg/proxmox provider
- **Secrets**: 1Password CLI (`op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"`)

## Documentation

- **[MIGRATION.md](tofu/MIGRATION.md)** - Guide for migrating apps to docker-lxc module pattern
- **[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)** - This file (project overview and quick reference)

## Project Structure

```text
tofu/
├── MIGRATION.md       # Migration guide for docker-lxc pattern
├── apps/              # Per-app configs with own state
│   ├── dashboards/    # Homepage + Dashy (ID: 201)
│   ├── immich/        # Photo management (ID: 304)
│   ├── monitoring/    # Prometheus + Grafana + Alerting (ID: 500)
│   ├── network-services/  # AdGuard DNS (ID: 101)
│   ├── openwebui/     # AI chat (ID: 501)
│   ├── portainer/     # Container UI (ID: 100)
│   └── traefik/       # Reverse proxy (ID: 200)
├── configs/traefik/dynamic/  # Generated route configs
├── modules/           # Reusable modules
└── shared.tf          # Common vars (symlinked)
```

## Key Modules

- **lxc-base**: Base LXC container with static IP support
- **docker-host**: LXC + Docker + compose deployment
- **file-sync**: Rsync file transfers to LXCs
- **proxmox-notes**: Update LXC description in Proxmox UI

## IP Address Management

All static IPs are tracked in `tofu/ip-registry.tf` (symlinked to all apps).

Based on the previous session, we need to mount `/tank/backups/pbs` from the Proxmox host to `/mnt/datastore` inside the PBS container. This is where PBS will store all the backup data.

After you finish the PBS installation script, run these commands:

```bash
# 1. Stop the container to add mount
ssh root@homelab "pct stop 102"

# 2. Disable protection temporarily
ssh root@homelab "pct set 102 -protection 0"

# 3. Create the ZFS dataset if it doesn't exist
ssh root@homelab "zfs create -p tank/backups/pbs" 

# 4. Add the mount point
ssh root@homelab "pct set 102 -mp0 /tank/backups/pbs,mp=/mnt/datastore"

# 5. Re-enable protection and start
ssh root@homelab "pct set 102 -protection 1 && pct start 102"
```

Then inside PBS:
```bash
# Create the datastore
ssh root@homelab "pct exec 102 -- proxmox-backup-manager datastore create homelab /mnt/datastore"

# Create prune job
ssh root@homelab "pct exec 102 -- proxmox-backup-manager prune-job create homelab-prune --store homelab --schedule '06:00' --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4 --keep-monthly 3"

# Set GC schedule
ssh root@homelab "pct exec 102 -- proxmox-backup-manager datastore update homelab --gc-schedule '05:00'"
```

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Usage:
#   1. When deploying a new service, check `local.next_available_ip` for the
#      next free IP in the LXC range (192.168.1.150-199)
#   2. Add the new allocation to the appropriate category below
#   3. Use `local.ip_registry.<category>.<name>` in your module configs
#
# Ranges:
#   - 192.168.1.1-99:     Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches)
#   - 192.168.1.100-149:  Core services (Traefik, Portainer, DNS)
#   - 192.168.1.150-199:  LXC containers (apps)
#   - 192.168.1.200-224:  Reserved for manual/temporary use
#   - 192.168.1.225-254:  Special services & overflow
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    netmask = "/24"
    prefix  = "192.168.1"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - All Static Allocations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure devices (1-99)
    infrastructure = {
      router           = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox          = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host
    }

    # Core services (100-149)
    core = {
      portainer        = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC 100 - Container management
      network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Unbound
      traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
    }

    # Application LXCs (150-199 preferred range for new deployments)
    apps = {
      dashboards       = "192.168.1.234"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia         = "192.168.1.225"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
      immich_importer  = "192.168.1.159"  # LXC 303 - Photo import (estimated)
      immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
      jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "192.168.1.227"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack (Radarr, Sonarr, etc)
      monitoring       = "192.168.1.229"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui        = "192.168.1.221"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n              = "192.168.1.213"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }

    # Reserved/Temporary containers (not managed by OpenTofu)
    reserved = {
      # 192.168.1.200-224 - Manual/temporary use
      # desktop_tmp = "DHCP"  # LXC 600 - Temporary GUI desktop (task desktop:create)
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for collision detection
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_allocated_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.infrastructure),
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.apps),
  )

  # Extract the last octet from each IP for range calculations
  _allocated_octets = [
    for ip in local._all_allocated_ips : tonumber(split(".", ip)[3])
  ]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Next Available IP Calculator
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Scans the preferred LXC range (150-199) for the next free IP.
  # Falls back to extended range (200-224) if primary is full.

  # Primary range: 150-199 (50 IPs for LXC apps)
  _primary_range = [for i in range(150, 200) : i]

  # Secondary range: 200-212 (for overflow, avoiding special services at 213+)
  _secondary_range = [for i in range(200, 213) : i]

  # Find first available in primary range
  _available_primary = [
    for octet in local._primary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # Find first available in secondary range
  _available_secondary = [
    for octet in local._secondary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # The next available IP (primary range first, then secondary)
  next_available_ip = length(local._available_primary) > 0 ? (
    "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_primary[0]}"
  ) : (
    length(local._available_secondary) > 0 ? (
      "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_secondary[0]}"
    ) : "NO_IPS_AVAILABLE"
  )

  # Full CIDR notation for direct use in lxc-base module
  next_available_ip_cidr = "${local.next_available_ip}${local.network.netmask}"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Usage: local.ip_cidr["dashboards"] -> "192.168.1.234/24"
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.infrastructure,
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.apps,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping (for reference)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    100 = local.ip_registry.core.portainer
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    200 = local.ip_registry.core.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.apps.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.apps.authelia
    303 = local.ip_registry.apps.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.apps.immich
    401 = local.ip_registry.apps.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.apps.media_management
    500 = local.ip_registry.apps.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.apps.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.apps.n8n
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "next_available_ip" {
  description = "Next available IP address for new LXC deployment"
  value       = local.next_available_ip
}

output "next_available_ip_cidr" {
  description = "Next available IP with CIDR notation (for lxc-base module)"
  value       = local.next_available_ip_cidr
}

output "allocated_ips" {
  description = "All currently allocated IP addresses"
  value       = local._all_allocated_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Usage:
#   1. When deploying a new service, check `local.next_available_ip` for the
#      next free IP in the LXC range (192.168.1.150-199)
#   2. Add the new allocation to the appropriate category below
#   3. Use `local.ip_registry.<category>.<name>` in your module configs
#
# Ranges:
#   - 192.168.1.1-99:     Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches)
#   - 192.168.1.100-149:  Core services (Traefik, Portainer, DNS)
#   - 192.168.1.150-199:  LXC containers (apps)
#   - 192.168.1.200-224:  Reserved for manual/temporary use
#   - 192.168.1.225-254:  Special services & overflow
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    netmask = "/24"
    prefix  = "192.168.1"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - All Static Allocations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure devices (1-99)
    infrastructure = {
      router           = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox          = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host
    }

    # Core services (100-149)
    core = {
      portainer        = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC 100 - Container management
      network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Unbound
      pbs              = "192.168.1.152"  # LXC 102 - Proxmox Backup Server
      traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
    }

    # Application LXCs (150-199 preferred range for new deployments)
    apps = {
      dashboards       = "192.168.1.234"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia         = "192.168.1.225"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
      immich_importer  = "192.168.1.159"  # LXC 303 - Photo import (estimated)
      immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
      jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "192.168.1.227"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack (Radarr, Sonarr, etc)
      monitoring       = "192.168.1.229"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui        = "192.168.1.221"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n              = "192.168.1.213"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }

    # Reserved/Temporary containers (not managed by OpenTofu)
    reserved = {
      # 192.168.1.200-224 - Manual/temporary use
      # desktop_tmp = "DHCP"  # LXC 600 - Temporary GUI desktop (task desktop:create)
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for collision detection
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_allocated_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.infrastructure),
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.apps),
  )

  # Extract the last octet from each IP for range calculations
  _allocated_octets = [
    for ip in local._all_allocated_ips : tonumber(split(".", ip)[3])
  ]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Next Available IP Calculator
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Scans the preferred LXC range (150-199) for the next free IP.
  # Falls back to extended range (200-224) if primary is full.

  # Primary range: 150-199 (50 IPs for LXC apps)
  _primary_range = [for i in range(150, 200) : i]

  # Secondary range: 200-212 (for overflow, avoiding special services at 213+)
  _secondary_range = [for i in range(200, 213) : i]

  # Find first available in primary range
  _available_primary = [
    for octet in local._primary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # Find first available in secondary range
  _available_secondary = [
    for octet in local._secondary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # The next available IP (primary range first, then secondary)
  next_available_ip = length(local._available_primary) > 0 ? (
    "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_primary[0]}"
  ) : (
    length(local._available_secondary) > 0 ? (
      "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_secondary[0]}"
    ) : "NO_IPS_AVAILABLE"
  )

  # Full CIDR notation for direct use in lxc-base module
  next_available_ip_cidr = "${local.next_available_ip}${local.network.netmask}"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Usage: local.ip_cidr["dashboards"] -> "192.168.1.234/24"
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.infrastructure,
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.apps,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping (for reference)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    100 = local.ip_registry.core.portainer
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    200 = local.ip_registry.core.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.apps.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.apps.authelia
    303 = local.ip_registry.apps.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.apps.immich
    401 = local.ip_registry.apps.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.apps.media_management
    500 = local.ip_registry.apps.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.apps.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.apps.n8n
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "next_available_ip" {
  description = "Next available IP address for new LXC deployment"
  value       = local.next_available_ip
}

output "next_available_ip_cidr" {
  description = "Next available IP with CIDR notation (for lxc-base module)"
  value       = local.next_available_ip_cidr
}

output "allocated_ips" {
  description = "All currently allocated IP addresses"
  value       = local._all_allocated_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

PBS is fully set up. Here's a summary:

**PBS Configuration:**
- **Container ID**: 102
- **IP**: 192.168.1.152
- **Web UI**: https://192.168.1.152:8007
- **Datastore**: `homelab` at `/mnt/datastore` (backed by `/tank/backups/pbs`)
- **PVE Storage**: `pbs-homelab` (~58GB available)
- **Prune Job**: Daily at 06:00 (keep 7 daily, 4 weekly, 3 monthly)
- **Garbage Collection**: Daily at 05:00

**To backup a container from Proxmox:**
```bash
# Via GUI: Datacenter > Storage > pbs-homelab > Backup Now
# Or via CLI:
vzdump <VMID> --storage pbs-homelab --mode snapshot
```

You can now use `pbs-homelab` as a backup destination in Proxmox for any container or VM.
so do we still need the backup scripts we created?

Good question. Let's compare what PBS provides vs the existing backup scripts:

**PBS handles:**
- Full LXC/VM backups (entire container snapshots)
- Incremental, deduplicated storage
- Automatic pruning and retention
- Point-in-time restore of whole containers

**Your existing backup scripts handle:**
- `vzdump` backups to `/tank/backups/vzdump` (now redundant with PBS)
- Immich PostgreSQL database dumps (pre-backup hook)
- rclone sync to Backblaze B2 for photos

**My recommendation:**

| Script | Keep? | Reason |
|--------|-------|--------|
| vzdump configs | **No** | PBS replaces this entirely |
| Immich DB dump | **Yes** | PBS backs up the container, but a pre-backup DB dump ensures consistency |
| rclone B2 sync | **Yes** | PBS is local-only; you still need offsite backup for photos |

So you can:
1. **Remove** the vzdump backup jobs/scripts
2. **Keep** the Immich pre-backup hook (move it to PBS as a pre-backup script)
3. **Keep** rclone for offsite photo backups

Want me to:
1. Check what backup scripts exist and identify which to remove?
2. Configure PBS to run a pre-backup script for Immich DB dumps?
and does PBS handle updating to backblaze as well?

No, PBS is local-only. It doesn't support cloud storage backends like Backblaze B2.

**PBS storage options:**
- Local directories
- ZFS datasets
- Remote PBS servers (PBS-to-PBS sync)

**For offsite/cloud backups, you still need rclone** (or similar) to sync to B2.

However, you have two strategies:

**Option A: rclone syncs photos directly (current)**
```
Immich photos → rclone → Backblaze B2
```

**Option B: PBS backup + rclone the PBS datastore**
```
LXC containers → PBS → /tank/backups/pbs → rclone → B2
```

Option B would back up entire containers (including databases, configs, everything) to B2, but:
- PBS uses a proprietary chunk format - you'd need PBS to restore
- Much larger storage usage on B2
- More complex restore process

**My recommendation:** Keep both systems:
1. **PBS** for local container backups (fast restore, point-in-time recovery)
2. **rclone** for offsite photo backups to B2 (disaster recovery for irreplaceable data)

The photos are the irreplaceable data. Container configs can be rebuilt from your OpenTofu code, but photos can't be recreated.

how long do the networks usually take to flush the stale entry?

ARP cache timeout varies by device:

| Device | Default ARP Timeout |
|--------|---------------------|
| Linux (Proxmox, LXCs) | 30-60 seconds (but can be refreshed if traffic flows) |
| macOS | 20 minutes |
| Windows | 2-10 minutes |
| Routers/Switches | 4-6 hours (sometimes longer) |

The problem is your router likely has the stale entry and keeps propagating it. Every time a device asks "who has 192.168.1.152?", the router may respond with the old MAC.

You could try:
1. **Reboot your router** - Clears its ARP cache immediately
2. **Wait 4-6 hours** - Let it expire naturally
3. **Fresh IP tomorrow** - Cleanest long-term fix

---

## Network Migration Plan: 192.168.1.x → 10.100.x.x

### IP Addressing Scheme

Align container IDs with IPs for easy tracking:

| Container ID Range | IP Range | Purpose |
|-------------------|----------|---------|
| 100-149 | 10.100.**1**.0-49 | Core services (Traefik, DNS, PBS, Portainer) |
| 200-249 | 10.100.**2**.0-49 | Dashboards & Auth |
| 300-349 | 10.100.**3**.0-49 | Media (Immich, Photos) |
| 400-449 | 10.100.**4**.0-49 | Media (Jellyfin, Arr stack) |
| 500-549 | 10.100.**5**.0-49 | Monitoring & AI |

**Example mapping:**
- LXC 100 (Portainer) → 10.100.1.100
- LXC 200 (Traefik) → 10.100.2.200
- LXC 304 (Immich) → 10.100.3.104
- LXC 500 (Monitoring) → 10.100.5.100

### Dual-Stack Migration (Safe Approach)

**Phase 1: Setup**
1. Create new bridge `vmbr1` on Proxmox for 10.100.0.0/16
2. Configure Proxmox as router between bridges
3. Add Tailscale route advertisement as backup

**Phase 2: Dual-NIC Migration (one container at a time)**
1. Add second NIC (10.100.x.x) to container
2. Update Traefik backend to use new IP
3. Test connectivity
4. Remove old 192.168.1.x NIC

**Phase 3: Exceptions (keep on 192.168.1.x)**
- Traefik: Needs 192.168.1.x for LAN clients
- AdGuard: DNS for LAN devices
- Jellyfin: DLNA/casting integration
- Immich: Mobile app sync

These get **dual NICs permanently** (one on each network).

### Network Topology

```
FIOS Router (192.168.1.1)
      │
      ├── 192.168.1.215 (Proxmox - vmbr0)
      │         │
      │         ├── vmbr1 (10.100.0.1) ← New bridge, Proxmox routes
      │         │      │
      │         │      └── All LXCs (10.100.x.x)
      │         │
      │         └── Dual-NIC containers:
      │               ├── Traefik (192.168.1.235 + 10.100.2.200)
      │               ├── AdGuard (192.168.1.196 + 10.100.1.101)
      │               ├── Jellyfin (192.168.1.226 + 10.100.4.101)
      │               └── Immich (192.168.1.222 + 10.100.3.104)
      │
      └── LAN devices (192.168.1.x) → access via Traefik
```

Yes, Tailscale can advertise multiple subnets. You just pass both to `--advertise-routes`:


This means from any Tailscale-connected device (your laptop, phone, etc.), you could reach both:
- `192.168.1.x` (home LAN)
- `10.100.x.x` (container network)

- Single point advertising both networks
- Already has access to both bridges

Option B: **Dedicated LXC** (cleaner separation)
- Container with dual NICs (one on each bridge)
- Advertises both subnets

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Usage:
#   1. When deploying a new service, check `local.next_available_ip` for the
#      next free IP in the LXC range (192.168.1.150-199)
#   2. Add the new allocation to the appropriate category below
#   3. Use `local.ip_registry.<category>.<name>` in your module configs
#
# Ranges:
#   - 192.168.1.1-99:     Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches)
#   - 192.168.1.100-149:  Core services (Traefik, Portainer, DNS)
#   - 192.168.1.150-199:  LXC containers (apps)
#   - 192.168.1.200-224:  Reserved for manual/temporary use
#   - 192.168.1.225-254:  Special services & overflow
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    netmask = "/24"
    prefix  = "192.168.1"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - All Static Allocations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure devices (1-99)
    infrastructure = {
      router           = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox          = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host
    }

    # Core services (100-149)
    core = {
      portainer        = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC 100 - Container management
      network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Unbound
      pbs              = "192.168.1.152"  # LXC 102 - Proxmox Backup Server
      traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
    }

    # Application LXCs (150-199 preferred range for new deployments)
    apps = {
      dashboards       = "192.168.1.234"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia         = "192.168.1.225"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
      immich_importer  = "192.168.1.159"  # LXC 303 - Photo import (estimated)
      immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
      jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "192.168.1.227"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack (Radarr, Sonarr, etc)
      monitoring       = "192.168.1.229"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui        = "192.168.1.221"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n              = "192.168.1.213"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }

    # Reserved/Temporary containers (not managed by OpenTofu)
    reserved = {
      # 192.168.1.200-224 - Manual/temporary use
      # desktop_tmp = "DHCP"  # LXC 600 - Temporary GUI desktop (task desktop:create)
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for collision detection
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_allocated_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.infrastructure),
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.apps),
  )

  # Extract the last octet from each IP for range calculations
  _allocated_octets = [
    for ip in local._all_allocated_ips : tonumber(split(".", ip)[3])
  ]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Next Available IP Calculator
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Scans the preferred LXC range (150-199) for the next free IP.
  # Falls back to extended range (200-224) if primary is full.

  # Primary range: 150-199 (50 IPs for LXC apps)
  _primary_range = [for i in range(150, 200) : i]

  # Secondary range: 200-212 (for overflow, avoiding special services at 213+)
  _secondary_range = [for i in range(200, 213) : i]

  # Find first available in primary range
  _available_primary = [
    for octet in local._primary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # Find first available in secondary range
  _available_secondary = [
    for octet in local._secondary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # The next available IP (primary range first, then secondary)
  next_available_ip = length(local._available_primary) > 0 ? (
    "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_primary[0]}"
  ) : (
    length(local._available_secondary) > 0 ? (
      "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_secondary[0]}"
    ) : "NO_IPS_AVAILABLE"
  )

  # Full CIDR notation for direct use in lxc-base module
  next_available_ip_cidr = "${local.next_available_ip}${local.network.netmask}"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Usage: local.ip_cidr["dashboards"] -> "192.168.1.234/24"
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.infrastructure,
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.apps,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping (for reference)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    100 = local.ip_registry.core.portainer
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    102 = local.ip_registry.core.pbs
    200 = local.ip_registry.core.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.apps.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.apps.authelia
    303 = local.ip_registry.apps.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.apps.immich
    401 = local.ip_registry.apps.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.apps.media_management
    500 = local.ip_registry.apps.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.apps.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.apps.n8n
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "next_available_ip" {
  description = "Next available IP address for new LXC deployment"
  value       = local.next_available_ip
}

output "next_available_ip_cidr" {
  description = "Next available IP with CIDR notation (for lxc-base module)"
  value       = local.next_available_ip_cidr
}

output "allocated_ips" {
  description = "All currently allocated IP addresses"
  value       = local._all_allocated_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Usage:
#   1. When deploying a new service, check `local.next_available_ip` for the
#      next free IP in the LXC range (192.168.1.150-199)
#   2. Add the new allocation to the appropriate category below
#   3. Use `local.ip_registry.<category>.<name>` in your module configs
#
# Ranges:
#   - 192.168.1.1-99:     Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches)
#   - 192.168.1.100-149:  Core services (Traefik, Portainer, DNS)
#   - 192.168.1.150-199:  LXC containers (apps)
#   - 192.168.1.200-224:  Reserved for manual/temporary use
#   - 192.168.1.225-254:  Special services & overflow
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    netmask = "/24"
    prefix  = "192.168.1"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - All Static Allocations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure devices (1-99)
    infrastructure = {
      router           = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox          = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host
    }

    # Core services (100-149)
    core = {
      portainer        = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC 100 - Container management
      network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Unbound
      pbs              = "192.168.1.152"  # LXC 102 - Proxmox Backup Server
      traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
    }

    # Application LXCs (150-199 preferred range for new deployments)
    apps = {
      dashboards       = "192.168.1.234"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia         = "192.168.1.225"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
      immich_importer  = "192.168.1.159"  # LXC 303 - Photo import (estimated)
      immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
      jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "192.168.1.227"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack (Radarr, Sonarr, etc)
      monitoring       = "192.168.1.229"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui        = "192.168.1.221"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n              = "192.168.1.213"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }

    # Reserved/Temporary containers (not managed by OpenTofu)
    reserved = {
      # 192.168.1.200-224 - Manual/temporary use
      # desktop_tmp = "DHCP"  # LXC 600 - Temporary GUI desktop (task desktop:create)
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for collision detection
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_allocated_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.infrastructure),
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.apps),
  )

  # Extract the last octet from each IP for range calculations
  _allocated_octets = [
    for ip in local._all_allocated_ips : tonumber(split(".", ip)[3])
  ]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Next Available IP Calculator
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Scans the preferred LXC range (150-199) for the next free IP.
  # Falls back to extended range (200-224) if primary is full.

  # Primary range: 150-199 (50 IPs for LXC apps)
  _primary_range = [for i in range(150, 200) : i]

  # Secondary range: 200-212 (for overflow, avoiding special services at 213+)
  _secondary_range = [for i in range(200, 213) : i]

  # Find first available in primary range
  _available_primary = [
    for octet in local._primary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # Find first available in secondary range
  _available_secondary = [
    for octet in local._secondary_range : octet
    if !contains(local._allocated_octets, octet)
  ]

  # The next available IP (primary range first, then secondary)
  next_available_ip = length(local._available_primary) > 0 ? (
    "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_primary[0]}"
  ) : (
    length(local._available_secondary) > 0 ? (
      "${local.network.prefix}.${local._available_secondary[0]}"
    ) : "NO_IPS_AVAILABLE"
  )

  # Full CIDR notation for direct use in lxc-base module
  next_available_ip_cidr = "${local.next_available_ip}${local.network.netmask}"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Usage: local.ip_cidr["dashboards"] -> "192.168.1.234/24"
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.infrastructure,
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.apps,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping (for reference)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    100 = local.ip_registry.core.portainer
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    102 = local.ip_registry.core.pbs
    200 = local.ip_registry.core.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.apps.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.apps.authelia
    303 = local.ip_registry.apps.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.apps.immich
    401 = local.ip_registry.apps.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.apps.media_management
    500 = local.ip_registry.apps.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.apps.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.apps.n8n
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "next_available_ip" {
  description = "Next available IP address for new LXC deployment"
  value       = local.next_available_ip
}

output "next_available_ip_cidr" {
  description = "Next available IP with CIDR notation (for lxc-base module)"
  value       = local.next_available_ip_cidr
}

output "allocated_ips" {
  description = "All currently allocated IP addresses"
  value       = local._all_allocated_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

what will the PVE's new IP address?

PVE (Proxmox host) will keep its current IP: **192.168.1.215**

It doesn't need to move to 10.100.x.x because:

3. You need LAN access to manage it

PVE has both IPs:

- **10.100.0.1** on vmbr1 (container gateway)

That's a solid phased approach. Let me clarify the PVE case though:

**PVE is special** - it's the physical host, not a container. It doesn't have an IP on the 10.100.x.x network in the same way containers do. The 10.100.0.1 is just the gateway address on vmbr1 - it's not a routable service IP.

So for PVE specifically, Traefik should continue using 192.168.1.215:8006.

**Migration Phases:**

| Phase | Action |
|-------|--------|
| **Phase 1** (done) | Create vmbr1, add dual-NIC to Traefik & network-services |
| **Phase 2** | Add eth1 (10.100.x.x) to all LXCs, update Traefik routes to use 10.100.x.x |
| **Phase 3** | Remove eth0 (192.168.1.x) from containers that don't need LAN access |

**Containers keeping 192.168.1.x (dual-NIC):**
- Traefik (LAN clients need to reach it)
- Network-services/AdGuard (DNS for LAN)
- Jellyfin (DLNA/casting)
- Immich (mobile app sync)

**Containers going 10.100.x.x only:**
- PBS, Portainer, Dashboards, Authelia, Monitoring, OpenWebUI, n8n, Media-management

Want me to start Phase 2 - adding the second NIC to remaining containers?
yes, but before that if I am on 192.x network say for example my TV and without tailscale, there is no way my tv can access 10.x ip right?

Correct. Devices on your 192.168.1.x network **cannot** reach 10.100.x.x directly without one of these:

1. **Tailscale** - which your TV likely doesn't have
2. **Router static route** - FIOS router would need to know "10.100.0.0/16 via 192.168.1.215"

But here's the thing - **they don't need to**. Your TV accesses services via Traefik using domain names like `jellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev`, which:

1. Resolves to **192.168.1.235** (Traefik's LAN IP via AdGuard DNS)
2. Traefik proxies to **10.100.x.x** backend (Traefik has both NICs)

```
TV (192.168.1.x)
    │
    ▼ DNS: jellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev → 192.168.1.235
    │
Traefik (192.168.1.235 + 10.100.4.101)
    │
    ▼ Proxy to backend
    │
Jellyfin (10.100.4.101)
```

So LAN devices only talk to Traefik on 192.168.1.235 - they never need to know about the 10.100.x.x network.

**Exception:** Jellyfin DLNA/casting might need direct LAN access (not proxied). That's why Jellyfin keeps its 192.168.1.x NIC.

Your router is configured with AdGuard (192.168.1.196) as the primary DNS. That's good - it means all LAN devices should get DNS from AdGuard.

Let me verify the DNS rewrite is working correctly and check what your TV might be seeing:

There's the problem. Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) is returning the **old** Traefik IP (192.168.1.162).

If your TV or any device falls back to the secondary DNS (1.1.1.1), it gets the wrong IP.

This means your **public DNS records** (on Cloudflare) still point to 192.168.1.162 instead of 192.168.1.235.

**Options:**

1. **Update Cloudflare DNS** - Change the A record for `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` from 192.168.1.162 to 192.168.1.235

2. **Remove secondary DNS** - Take 1.1.1.1 off your router so devices only use AdGuard (not ideal for reliability)

Do you want me to help update the Cloudflare DNS record?
will this dns change be part of cloudflare tunnel or a regular cloudflare record?

It's a **regular Cloudflare DNS record**, not the tunnel.

**How they differ:**

| Type | Purpose | Your setup |
|------|---------|------------|
| **Cloudflare Tunnel** | Public access (external → homelab) | `*.rambtech.dev` (no subdomain) |
| **Cloudflare DNS A record** | Internal LAN resolution fallback | `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` → 192.168.1.x |

The `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` A record exists so that if a device bypasses AdGuard and queries public DNS, it still gets an IP that works on your LAN.

Since this is internal-only, you could also just:
1. **Delete the public A record** for `*.homelab.rambtech.dev`
2. Rely solely on AdGuard DNS rewrites for LAN resolution

That way there's no stale public record to maintain. Devices not using AdGuard simply won't resolve `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` at all (which is fine - they shouldn't be accessing it anyway).

Which approach do you prefer?

2. Delete the A record entirely (AdGuard-only)
I went with option A so that if things in my local network bypass adguard for reasones like adguard not being available, we can still resolve to traefik

# =============================================================================
# Docker LXC Module
# =============================================================================
# Opinionated module for deploying Docker-based applications in LXC containers.
# Uses lxc-base + filesync provider + remotedockercompose provider for a
# fully declarative deployment experience.
# =============================================================================

terraform {
  required_providers {
    proxmox = {
      source  = "bpg/proxmox"
      version = "~> 0.69"
    }
    filesync = {
      source  = "darshan-rambhia/filesync"
      version = "~> 0.3"
    }
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LXC Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "lxc" {
  source = "../lxc-base"

  name         = var.name
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network
  ip_address     = var.ip_address
  gateway        = var.gateway
  network_bridge = "vmbr0"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Container type
  unprivileged = var.unprivileged
  template     = var.template

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key               = var.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Features
  enable_nesting = true
  enable_keyctl  = true
  enable_fuse    = false

  # Mount points
  mount_points = var.mount_points

  # Proxmox notes
  description = var.enable_proxmox_notes ? templatefile("${path.module}/templates/notes.md.tftpl", {
    service_name = var.service_name != "" ? var.service_name : var.name
    description  = var.service_description
    urls         = var.service_urls
    services     = var.services
    ssh_host     = split("/", var.ip_address)[0]
    custom_notes = var.custom_notes
    managed_by   = true
  }) : ""

  # Tags
  tags = concat(["docker"], var.tags)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File Sync - Using filesync provider directly
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Get list of all files in deploy directory, excluding specified patterns
locals {
  _all_deploy_files = var.deploy_dir != "" ? fileset(var.deploy_dir, "**") : []

  # Filter out files matching exclude patterns
  deploy_files = [
    for f in local._all_deploy_files : f
    if !anytrue([for pattern in var.exclude_patterns : can(regex(pattern, f))])
  ]
}

# Sync each file individually using filesync provider
resource "filesync_file" "config_files" {
  for_each = toset(local.deploy_files)

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${each.value}"
  destination = "${var.target_path}/${each.value}"
  host        = module.lxc.ip_address
  mode        = "0644"

  # SSH configuration - provider config is inherited but explicit for clarity
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [module.lxc]
}

# Set custom permissions for specific files
resource "filesync_file" "custom_permissions" {
  for_each = var.file_permissions

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${trimsuffix(trimprefix(each.key, var.target_path), "/")}"
  destination = each.key
  host        = module.lxc.ip_address
  mode        = each.value

  # SSH configuration
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [filesync_file.config_files]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Docker Compose
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Note: Docker Compose stack deployment is handled by the deploy directory
# containing docker-compose.yml. The filesync provider syncs the compose file
# to the container. Applications can manually run `docker compose up -d` via
# SSH if needed, or include it in post_sync_commands.

# =============================================================================
# Docker LXC Module
# =============================================================================
# Opinionated module for deploying Docker-based applications in LXC containers.
# Uses lxc-base + filesync provider + remotedockercompose provider for a
# fully declarative deployment experience.
# =============================================================================

terraform {
  required_providers {
    proxmox = {
      source  = "bpg/proxmox"
      version = "~> 0.69"
    }
    filesync = {
      source  = "darshan-rambhia/filesync"
      version = "~> 0.3"
    }
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LXC Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "lxc" {
  source = "../lxc-base"

  name         = var.name
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network - dual-network architecture
  container_ip      = var.container_ip
  container_gateway = var.container_gateway
  lan_ip            = var.lan_ip
  lan_gateway       = var.lan_gateway

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Container type
  unprivileged = var.unprivileged
  template     = var.template

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key               = var.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Features
  enable_nesting = true
  enable_keyctl  = true
  enable_fuse    = false

  # Mount points
  mount_points = var.mount_points

  # Proxmox notes
  description = var.enable_proxmox_notes ? templatefile("${path.module}/templates/notes.md.tftpl", {
    service_name = var.service_name != "" ? var.service_name : var.name
    description  = var.service_description
    urls         = var.service_urls
    services     = var.services
    ssh_host     = split("/", var.container_ip)[0]
    custom_notes = var.custom_notes
    managed_by   = true
  }) : ""

  # Tags
  tags = concat(["docker"], var.tags)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File Sync - Using filesync provider directly
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Get list of all files in deploy directory, excluding specified patterns
locals {
  _all_deploy_files = var.deploy_dir != "" ? fileset(var.deploy_dir, "**") : []

  # Filter out files matching exclude patterns
  deploy_files = [
    for f in local._all_deploy_files : f
    if !anytrue([for pattern in var.exclude_patterns : can(regex(pattern, f))])
  ]
}

# Sync each file individually using filesync provider
resource "filesync_file" "config_files" {
  for_each = toset(local.deploy_files)

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${each.value}"
  destination = "${var.target_path}/${each.value}"
  host        = module.lxc.ip_address
  mode        = "0644"

  # SSH configuration - provider config is inherited but explicit for clarity
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [module.lxc]
}

# Set custom permissions for specific files
resource "filesync_file" "custom_permissions" {
  for_each = var.file_permissions

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${trimsuffix(trimprefix(each.key, var.target_path), "/")}"
  destination = each.key
  host        = module.lxc.ip_address
  mode        = each.value

  # SSH configuration
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [filesync_file.config_files]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Docker Compose
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Note: Docker Compose stack deployment is handled by the deploy directory
# containing docker-compose.yml. The filesync provider syncs the compose file
# to the container. Applications can manually run `docker compose up -d` via
# SSH if needed, or include it in post_sync_commands.

# =============================================================================
# Traefik LXC - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 200
# IP: 192.168.1.235
#
# This deployment uses the docker-lxc module which handles:
#   1. LXC container creation with Docker pre-installed
#   2. File sync via rsync (file-sync module)
#   3. Docker Compose deployment
#   4. Proxmox notes generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App-specific Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Traefik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 200
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 2048
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
}

variable "rootfs_storage" {
  description = "Storage pool for root filesystem"
  type        = string
  default     = "nvme-containers"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "traefik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network
  ip_address = "${local.ip_registry.core.traefik}/24"
  gateway    = "192.168.1.1"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude migrated routes (managed by traefik-route module) and env templates (env is generated)
  exclude_patterns = ["^migrated-dynamic/", "^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Traefik"
  service_description = "Reverse proxy and ingress controller for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
    direct             = "http://${local.ip_registry.core.traefik}:8080/dashboard/"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "HTTP", port = 80, info = "HTTP entrypoint (redirects to HTTPS)" },
    { name = "HTTPS", port = 443, info = "HTTPS entrypoint with Let's Encrypt" },
    { name = "Metrics", port = 8082, info = "Prometheus metrics endpoint" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  tags = ["traefik", "ingress", "reverse-proxy"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "traefik_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    cf_api_token = local.op.cloudflare_api_token
    cf_api_email = "darshanrambhia@live.com"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/traefik.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "traefik_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.traefik_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = local.ip_registry.core.traefik

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.traefik.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.traefik.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.traefik.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Traefik LXC - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 200
# IP: 192.168.1.235
#
# This deployment uses the docker-lxc module which handles:
#   1. LXC container creation with Docker pre-installed
#   2. File sync via rsync (file-sync module)
#   3. Docker Compose deployment
#   4. Proxmox notes generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App-specific Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Traefik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 200
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 2048
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
}

variable "rootfs_storage" {
  description = "Storage pool for root filesystem"
  type        = string
  default     = "nvme-containers"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "traefik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network
  ip_address = "${local.ip_registry.core.traefik}/24"
  gateway    = "192.168.1.1"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude migrated routes (managed by traefik-route module) and env templates (env is generated)
  exclude_patterns = ["^migrated-dynamic/", "^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Traefik"
  service_description = "Reverse proxy and ingress controller for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
    direct             = "http://${local.ip_registry.core.traefik}:8080/dashboard/"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "HTTP", port = 80, info = "HTTP entrypoint (redirects to HTTPS)" },
    { name = "HTTPS", port = 443, info = "HTTPS entrypoint with Let's Encrypt" },
    { name = "Metrics", port = 8082, info = "Prometheus metrics endpoint" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  tags = ["traefik", "ingress", "reverse-proxy"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "traefik_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    cf_api_token = local.op.cloudflare_api_token
    cf_api_email = "darshanrambhia@live.com"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/traefik.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "traefik_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.traefik_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = local.ip_registry.core.traefik

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.traefik.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.traefik.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.traefik.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
  }
}

Now I have a clear picture. Let me compare which routes are managed by traefik-route module vs centralized:

**Routes managed by traefik-route module (per-app):**
- portainer, dns, photos, qbittorrent, sonarr, radarr, lidarr, prowlarr, bazarr, sabnzbd, openwebui, jellyfin, homepage, dashy, grafana, prometheus, alertmanager, status, ntfy, n8n, authelia

**Centralized routes in `tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/`:**
- alertmanager.yml, authelia.yml, bazarr.yml, common.yml, dashy.yml, dns.yml, grafana.yml, homepage.yml, jellyfin.yml, jellystat.yml, lidarr.yml, n8n.yml, ntfy.yml, openwebui.yml, pbs.yml, photos.yml, portainer.yml, prometheus.yml, prowlarr.yml, pve.yml, qbittorrent.yml, radarr.yml, requests.yml, sabnzbd.yml, sonarr.yml, status.yml, traefik.yml

1. The traefik-route module generates and syncs routes to the Traefik LXC
2. The centralized files are also synced via docker-lxc module
3. Both are writing to `/config/dynamic/` on Traefik

Now I have a complete understanding. Here's the situation:

**Routes that MUST stay centralized** (not managed by any app's OpenTofu):
- `common.yml` - Shared middlewares (security-headers, public-security, internal-only)
- `traefik.yml` - Traefik dashboard route (uses api@internal service)
- `pve.yml` - Proxmox VE UI (192.168.1.215, not an OpenTofu-managed app)
- `pbs.yml` - Proxmox Backup Server (10.100.1.102, not an OpenTofu-managed app)

**Routes that are duplicated** (managed by traefik-route module AND centralized):
- alertmanager.yml, authelia.yml, bazarr.yml, dashy.yml, dns.yml, grafana.yml, homepage.yml, jellyfin.yml, lidarr.yml, n8n.yml, ntfy.yml, openwebui.yml, photos.yml, portainer.yml, prometheus.yml, prowlarr.yml, qbittorrent.yml, radarr.yml, sabnzbd.yml, sonarr.yml, status.yml

**Routes only in centralized** (Jellyfin sub-services):
- `jellystat.yml` - Points to 10.100.4.101:3000 (Jellyfin LXC)

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Network Architecture:
#   - 192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0): Home LAN - FIOS router, external access
#   - 10.100.0.0/16  (vmbr1): Container network - internal services
#
# IP Scheme (Container ID aligned with IP):
#   - 10.100.1.x:  Core services (LXC 100-149)
#   - 10.100.2.x:  Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249)
#   - 10.100.3.x:  Media - Photos (LXC 300-349)
#   - 10.100.4.x:  Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449)
#   - 10.100.5.x:  Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549)
#
# Dual-NIC Services (need 192.168.1.x for LAN compatibility):
#   - Traefik: Reverse proxy for LAN clients
#   - AdGuard: DNS for LAN devices
#   - Jellyfin: DLNA/casting
#   - Immich: Mobile app sync
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    # Home LAN (vmbr0)
    lan_gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    lan_netmask = "/24"
    lan_prefix  = "192.168.1"

    # Container network (vmbr1)
    container_gateway = "10.100.0.1"
    container_netmask = "/16"
    container_prefix  = "10.100"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - Container Network (10.100.x.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pattern: 10.100.<category>.<container_id_suffix>
  # Example: LXC 304 -> 10.100.3.104 (category 3, suffix 04)

  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure (192.168.1.x only - not containers)
    infrastructure = {
      router  = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host (vmbr0)
      # Proxmox also has 10.100.0.1 on vmbr1 (gateway for containers)
    }

    # Core services (LXC 100-149) -> 10.100.1.x
    core = {
      portainer        = "10.100.1.100"  # LXC 100 - Container management
      network_services = "10.100.1.101"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Tailscale
      pbs              = "10.100.1.102"  # LXC 102 - Proxmox Backup Server
    }

    # Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249) -> 10.100.2.x
    dashboards = {
      traefik    = "10.100.2.200"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
      dashboards = "10.100.2.201"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia   = "10.100.2.202"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
    }

    # Media - Photos (LXC 300-349) -> 10.100.3.x
    photos = {
      immich_importer = "10.100.3.103"  # LXC 303 - Photo import
      immich          = "10.100.3.104"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
    }

    # Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449) -> 10.100.4.x
    media = {
      jellyfin         = "10.100.4.101"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "10.100.4.102"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack
    }

    # Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549) -> 10.100.5.x
    monitoring = {
      monitoring = "10.100.5.100"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui  = "10.100.5.101"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n        = "10.100.5.102"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # LAN IPs for Dual-NIC Services (192.168.1.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # These services need direct LAN access for compatibility with home devices

  lan_ips = {
    traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - LAN clients access services
    network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - DNS for LAN devices
    jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - DLNA/casting
    immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Mobile app sync
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    # Core (100-149)
    100 = local.ip_registry.core.portainer
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    102 = local.ip_registry.core.pbs

    # Dashboards & Auth (200-249)
    200 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.authelia

    # Photos (300-349)
    303 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich

    # Media (400-449)
    401 = local.ip_registry.media.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.media.media_management

    # Monitoring & AI (500-549)
    500 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.dashboards,
      local.ip_registry.photos,
      local.ip_registry.media,
      local.ip_registry.monitoring,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  }

  lan_ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in local.lan_ips : name => "${ip}${local.network.lan_netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for validation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_container_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.dashboards),
    values(local.ip_registry.photos),
    values(local.ip_registry.media),
    values(local.ip_registry.monitoring),
  )

  _all_lan_ips = values(local.lan_ips)
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "container_ips" {
  description = "All container IPs (10.100.x.x)"
  value       = local._all_container_ips
}

output "lan_ips" {
  description = "LAN IPs for dual-NIC services (192.168.1.x)"
  value       = local.lan_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

output "network" {
  description = "Network configuration"
  value       = local.network
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 100
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 16
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
