module "portainer" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "portainer"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network
  ip_address = "${local.ip_registry.core.portainer}/24"
  gateway    = "192.168.1.1"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 512

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for Docker
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Portainer"
  service_description = "Central Docker container management UI with Watchtower auto-updates"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://portainer.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.ip_registry.core.portainer}:9000"

Run `task tofu:apply APP=portainer` to update.

  tags = ["portainer", "management", "watchtower"]
}

}

  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.portainer_route.remote_config_path
}

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Network Architecture:
#   - 192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0): Home LAN - FIOS router, external access
#   - 10.100.0.0/16  (vmbr1): Container network - internal services
#
# IP Scheme (Container ID aligned with IP):
#   - 10.100.1.x:  Core services (LXC 100-149)
#   - 10.100.2.x:  Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249)
#   - 10.100.3.x:  Media - Photos (LXC 300-349)
#   - 10.100.4.x:  Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449)
#   - 10.100.5.x:  Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549)
#
# Dual-NIC Services (need 192.168.1.x for LAN compatibility):
#   - Traefik: Reverse proxy for LAN clients
#   - AdGuard: DNS for LAN devices
#   - Jellyfin: DLNA/casting
#   - Immich: Mobile app sync
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    # Home LAN (vmbr0)
    lan_gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    lan_netmask = "/24"
    lan_prefix  = "192.168.1"

    # Container network (vmbr1)
    container_gateway = "10.100.0.1"
    container_netmask = "/16"
    container_prefix  = "10.100"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - Container Network (10.100.x.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pattern: 10.100.<category>.<container_id_suffix>
  # Example: LXC 304 -> 10.100.3.104 (category 3, suffix 04)

  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure (192.168.1.x only - not containers)
    infrastructure = {
      router  = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host (vmbr0)
      # Proxmox also has 10.100.0.1 on vmbr1 (gateway for containers)
    }

    # Core services (LXC 100-149) -> 10.100.1.x
    core = {
      portainer        = "10.100.1.100"  # LXC 100 - Container management
      network_services = "10.100.1.101"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Tailscale
      pbs              = "10.100.1.102"  # LXC 102 - Proxmox Backup Server
    }

    # Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249) -> 10.100.2.x
    dashboards = {
      traefik    = "10.100.2.200"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
      dashboards = "10.100.2.201"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia   = "10.100.2.202"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
    }

    # Media - Photos (LXC 300-349) -> 10.100.3.x
    photos = {
      immich_importer = "10.100.3.103"  # LXC 303 - Photo import
      immich          = "10.100.3.104"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
    }

    # Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449) -> 10.100.4.x
    media = {
      jellyfin         = "10.100.4.101"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "10.100.4.102"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack
    }

    # Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549) -> 10.100.5.x
    monitoring = {
      monitoring = "10.100.5.100"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui  = "10.100.5.101"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n        = "10.100.5.102"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # LAN IPs for Dual-NIC Services (192.168.1.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # These services need direct LAN access for compatibility with home devices

  lan_ips = {
    traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - LAN clients access services
    network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - DNS for LAN devices
    jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - DLNA/casting
    immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Mobile app sync
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    # Core (100-149)
    100 = local.ip_registry.core.portainer
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    102 = local.ip_registry.core.pbs

    # Dashboards & Auth (200-249)
    200 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.authelia

    # Photos (300-349)
    303 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich

    # Media (400-449)
    401 = local.ip_registry.media.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.media.media_management

    # Monitoring & AI (500-549)
    500 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.dashboards,
      local.ip_registry.photos,
      local.ip_registry.media,
      local.ip_registry.monitoring,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  }

  lan_ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in local.lan_ips : name => "${ip}${local.network.lan_netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for validation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_container_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.dashboards),
    values(local.ip_registry.photos),
    values(local.ip_registry.media),
    values(local.ip_registry.monitoring),
  )

  _all_lan_ips = values(local.lan_ips)
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "container_ips" {
  description = "All container IPs (10.100.x.x)"
  value       = local._all_container_ips
}

output "lan_ips" {
  description = "LAN IPs for dual-NIC services (192.168.1.x)"
  value       = local.lan_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

output "network" {
  description = "Network configuration"
  value       = local.network
}

content.text:
I need to update all apps to use the new dual-network architecture. Let me read the docker-lxc variables to understand the new pattern:

The new pattern is:
- `container_ip` = "10.100.x.x/16" (required, goes on eth0/vmbr1)
- `container_gateway` = "10.100.0.1" (default)
- `lan_ip` = "192.168.1.x/24" (optional, for dual-NIC services)
- `lan_gateway` = "192.168.1.1" (default)

Let me update all apps. I'll handle them in groups:

**Apps needing dual-NIC (lan_ip):**
- traefik
- network-services
- jellyfin
- immich

**Apps with container network only:**
- portainer
- dashboards
- authelia
- monitoring
- openwebui
- n8n
- media-management
- immich-importer

module "dashboards" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "dashboards"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network
  ip_address = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.dashboards}/24"
  gateway    = "192.168.1.1"

  # Resources

  memory = var.memory

    { name = "Homepage", port = 3000, info = "Main dashboard" },
    { name = "Dashy", port = 4001, info = "Alternative dashboard" },

# =============================================================================
# OpenWebUI LXC - AI Chat Interface with Ollama
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 501
# IP: 192.168.1.221
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Features AMD GPU passthrough for Ollama LLM acceleration.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network
  ip_address = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}/24"
  gateway    = "192.168.1.1"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for Docker
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with Ollama backend (AMD GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://192.168.1.221:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "Ollama", port = 11434, info = "LLM backend (ROCM GPU)" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M passed through for Ollama LLM acceleration:
- `/dev/kfd`, `/dev/dri` devices
- ROCM backend

**Check GPU:**
```
docker exec ollama rocminfo
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f openwebui
cd /config && docker compose logs -f ollama
```

**List models:**
```
docker exec ollama ollama list
```

**Pull new model:**
```
docker exec ollama ollama pull llama3.2
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "ollama", "llm"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.openwebui_route.internal_url
    direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.openwebui_route.remote_config_path
}

- **immich-go**: Google Photos importer
- **rclone**: Cloud backup to B2 (encrypted)

## Management

- SSH: `ssh root@${local.ip_registry.photos.immich_importer}`

## Cloud Backup

**Schedule:** ${var.cloud_backup_schedule} (Wed and Sun 3 AM EST)

**Commands:**
```bash
task cloud:sync:photos
task cloud:status:photos
task cloud:logs:photos
```

## Manual Import

**Run immich-go:**
```bash
immich-go -server ${var.immich_server} upload /downloads
```

## Rclone Status

**Check B2 sync status:**
```bash
/usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh status
```

**Manual sync:**
```bash
/usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh photos
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=immich-importer` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["immich-importer", "backup", "rclone", "opentofu"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wait for container to be ready
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "time_sleep" "wait_for_container" {
  depends_on      = [module.lxc]
  create_duration = "10s"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Install Dependencies (rclone, immich-go)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "null_resource" "install_dependencies" {
  depends_on = [time_sleep.wait_for_container]

  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
  }

  connection {
    type        = "ssh"
    host        = module.lxc.ip_address
    user        = "root"
    private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      "export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive",
      "apt-get update -qq",
      "apt-get install -y -qq curl unzip cron",

      # Install rclone
      "if ! command -v rclone &>/dev/null; then curl -fsSL https://rclone.org/install.sh | bash; fi",

      # Install immich-go (latest release)
      "if ! command -v immich-go &>/dev/null; then",
      "  IMMICH_GO_VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/simulot/immich-go/releases/latest | grep tag_name | cut -d'\"' -f4)",
      "  curl -fsSL https://github.com/simulot/immich-go/releases/download/$${IMMICH_GO_VERSION}/immich-go_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz | tar -xzf - -C /usr/local/bin immich-go",
      "  chmod +x /usr/local/bin/immich-go",
      "fi",

      # Create directories
      "mkdir -p /root/.config/rclone",
      "mkdir -p /var/log",
    ]
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configure rclone
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "null_resource" "configure_rclone" {
  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]

  triggers = {
    container_id    = var.container_id
    b2_account_id   = var.b2_account_id
    crypt_password  = var.rclone_crypt_password
    crypt_password2 = var.rclone_crypt_password2
  }

  connection {
    type        = "ssh"
    host        = module.lxc.ip_address
    user        = "root"
    private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      <<-RCLONE
      cat > /root/.config/rclone/rclone.conf << 'CONF'
[b2]
type = b2
account = ${var.b2_account_id}
key = ${var.b2_application_key}
hard_delete = true

[b2-crypt]
type = crypt
remote = b2:rambtech-homelab/photos-encrypted
password = ${var.rclone_crypt_password}
password2 = ${var.rclone_crypt_password2}
CONF
      chmod 600 /root/.config/rclone/rclone.conf
      RCLONE
    ]
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deploy Cloud Sync Script
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "null_resource" "deploy_cloud_sync" {
  depends_on = [null_resource.configure_rclone]

  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
    script_hash  = filesha256("${path.module}/deploy/cloud-sync.sh")
  }

  connection {
    type        = "ssh"
    host        = module.lxc.ip_address
    user        = "root"
    private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
  }

  provisioner "file" {
    source      = "${path.module}/deploy/cloud-sync.sh"
    destination = "/usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh"
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      "chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh"
    ]
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configure Cron Job for Cloud Backup
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "null_resource" "configure_cron" {
  depends_on = [null_resource.deploy_cloud_sync]

  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
    schedule     = var.cloud_backup_schedule
  }

  connection {
    type        = "ssh"
    host        = module.lxc.ip_address
    user        = "root"
    private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      # Remove existing cloud-sync cron entries
      "crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -v 'cloud-sync.sh' | crontab - || true",

      # Add new cron entry
      "(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '${var.cloud_backup_schedule} /usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh photos >> /var/log/cloud-sync-photos.log 2>&1') | crontab -",

      # Ensure cron service is running
      "systemctl enable cron",
      "systemctl start cron",

      "echo 'Cron configured: ${var.cloud_backup_schedule}'"
    ]
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.lxc.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.lxc.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.lxc.ssh_command
}

output "cloud_backup_schedule" {
  value = var.cloud_backup_schedule
}

# =============================================================================
# Traefik LXC - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 200
# IP: 192.168.1.235
#
# This deployment uses the docker-lxc module which handles:
#   1. LXC container creation with Docker pre-installed
#   2. File sync via rsync (file-sync module)
#   3. Docker Compose deployment
#   4. Proxmox notes generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App-specific Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Traefik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 200
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 2048
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
}

variable "rootfs_storage" {
  description = "Storage pool for root filesystem"
  type        = string
  default     = "nvme-containers"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "traefik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network
  ip_address = "${local.traefik_ip}/24"
  gateway    = "192.168.1.1"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude migrated routes (managed by traefik-route module) and env templates (env is generated)
  exclude_patterns = ["^migrated-dynamic/", "^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Traefik"
  service_description = "Reverse proxy and ingress controller for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
    direct             = "http://${local.traefik_ip}:8080/dashboard/"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "HTTP", port = 80, info = "HTTP entrypoint (redirects to HTTPS)" },
    { name = "HTTPS", port = 443, info = "HTTPS entrypoint with Let's Encrypt" },
    { name = "Metrics", port = 8082, info = "Prometheus metrics endpoint" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  tags = ["traefik", "ingress", "reverse-proxy"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "traefik_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    cf_api_token = local.op.cloudflare_api_token
    cf_api_email = "darshanrambhia@live.com"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/traefik.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "traefik_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.traefik_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = local.traefik_ip

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.traefik.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.traefik.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.traefik.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
  }
}

as for phase 3, why dont we handle that from opentofu directly applying the plan?

You're right - since we've already updated all the OpenTofu configurations to use the new `container_ip`/`lan_ip` variables, applying the plans will handle Phase 3 automatically. When OpenTofu applies, it will:

1. For **container-network-only apps** (portainer, dashboards, authelia, monitoring, openwebui, media-management, n8n, immich-importer): The LXC will be reconfigured with only eth0 on vmbr1 (10.100.x.x)

2. For **dual-NIC apps** (traefik, network-services, jellyfin, immich): The LXC will have eth0 on vmbr1 (10.100.x.x) and eth1 on vmbr0 (192.168.1.x)

However, there's one caveat - looking at the lxc-base module's lifecycle block, it has `ignore_changes` on `initialization` and `network_interface` which means existing containers won't have their network changed via OpenTofu apply. The changes will only apply to newly created containers.

For existing containers, we have two options:

1. **Destroy and recreate** - `tofu destroy` then `tofu apply` (loses container data)
2. **Manual migration** - Keep the current manual network changes we already did on Proxmox

Since we already manually added the 10.100.x.x NICs to all containers during Phase 2, the containers are already configured correctly. The OpenTofu state just needs to reflect the current reality.

Would you like me to:
1. **Remove the network-related items from `ignore_changes`** so future `tofu apply` can manage networks (risky for existing containers)
2. **Leave as-is** - The containers are already configured correctly manually, and new containers will use the correct IaC config
3. **Import the current state** for each container to sync OpenTofu with reality

Option 2 is safest since everything is already working. The IaC is now correct for any new deployments.
whats the harm in removing `network_interface` from the ignore_changes block? we had originally put it in there since PI was managed by dhcp so ip changes caused unnecessary drift

Good point - the original reason for ignoring `network_interface` was DHCP-related drift, but now we're using static IPs on a dedicated container network. Removing it should be safe and beneficial.

I notice `network_interface` isn't actually in the ignore_changes list - it must have been removed already or was never there. Let me check if `initialization` is the issue since it contains the IP config:

Looking at the lifecycle block, the relevant items are:
- `initialization` - This includes the IP configuration (`ip_config` block)
- `network_interface` - Not currently ignored

The `initialization` block is ignored because it contains `user_account.keys` and `hostname` which are create-time-only. However, the IP addresses are also in `initialization.ip_config`.

The problem is that `initialization` is a compound block - we can't selectively ignore parts of it. If we want OpenTofu to manage IP changes, we'd need to remove `initialization` from ignore_changes, but that could cause issues with SSH keys and hostname.

content.text: Portainer is fully migrated. Let me verify it's accessible:

Portainer is working. The migration process works, but there's one issue: the `initialization` block (which contains the IP config) is in `ignore_changes`, so OpenTofu can't update the IP directly via the API. We need to manually update each container's IP via `pct set` command.

Given this, let me create a quick script to migrate all remaining apps. The pattern is:
1. Run `tofu plan` to update state
2. Manually update network via `pct set`
3. Restart container
4. Run `tofu apply` to sync files and routes

Would you like me to proceed with migrating the rest of the apps this way, or would you prefer to do it gradually?
i dont think filesync has a bug, changing IP usually means a different host.

You're right - changing the host IP fundamentally changes the resource identity for filesync. It's not a bug, it's correct behavior - syncing to `192.168.1.150` vs `10.100.1.100` are different destinations from the provider's perspective.

The issue is that the state has the old IP in the resource ID. The cleanest approach is to let OpenTofu recreate those resources (which it did on the second apply).

Let me proceed with migrating the rest of the apps. I'll create a script to handle them all:

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The conversation is summarized below:
Analysis:
Let me analyze the conversation chronologically to capture all important details:

1. **Initial Context**: This conversation is a continuation from a previous session about PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) setup and network architecture changes - moving from 192.168.1.x to 10.100.x.x for containers.

2. **Traefik Route Management Cleanup**:
   - User raised concern about drift from duplicated routes in `tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/`
   - I analyzed which routes were managed by traefik-route module vs centralized
   - Moved 21+ duplicated routes to `migrated-dynamic/` folder
   - Kept only essential centralized routes: common.yml, traefik.yml, pve.yml, pbs.yml
   - Added jellystat and requests routes to jellyfin app

3. **IP Registry and Module Fixes**:
   - Fixed invalid `local.ip_registry.core.traefik` references → `local.traefik_ip`
   - Fixed `local.ip_registry.apps.*` references to correct category paths
   - Added `local.traefik_ip` convenience variable

4. **Network Configuration Migration**:
   - Updated all apps from old `ip_address`/`gateway` to new `container_ip`/`lan_ip` variables
   - Single-NIC apps: portainer, dashboards, authelia, monitoring, openwebui, media-management, n8n, immich-importer
   - Dual-NIC apps: traefik, network-services, jellyfin, immich

5. **Phase 3 Discussion**:
   - User asked about handling Phase 3 (removing old NICs) via OpenTofu
   - Discovered `network_interface` is NOT in ignore_changes
   - But `initialization` (containing IP config) IS ignored
   - This means bridge changes apply but IP changes don't via API

6. **User Feedback on filesync "bug"**:
   - I initially called the filesync provider error a "bug"
   - User corrected me: "i dont think filesync has a bug, changing IP usually means a different host"
   - User was right - changing host fundamentally changes resource identity

7. **Actual Migration Execution**:
   - Manually migrated portainer's network via `pct set`
   - Then ran `tofu apply` to sync state and routes
   - Migrated all remaining containers via SSH to Proxmox
   - Applied OpenTofu for each app to sync routes

8. **Current State**:
   - All containers migrated to new network
   - portainer, dashboards, traefik, monitoring successfully applied
   - Still need to apply remaining apps: authelia, openwebui, n8n, media-management, network-services, jellyfin, immich

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user's requests evolved through this session:
   - Clean up Traefik route management to prevent drift (routes managed by both centralized files AND traefik-route module)
   - Update IaC to reflect new dual-network architecture (10.100.x.x container network + 192.168.1.x LAN)
   - Execute Phase 3 of network migration: actually apply the network changes to containers via OpenTofu
   - User specifically asked: "as for phase 3, why dont we handle that from opentofu directly applying the plan?"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Dual-network architecture: vmbr1 (10.100.x.x containers) + vmbr0 (192.168.1.x LAN)
   - traefik-route module for per-app route management
   - OpenTofu lifecycle `ignore_changes` for `initialization` block (prevents IP changes via API)
   - `pct set` commands for manual network configuration
   - filesync provider resource identity based on host IP
   - Container ID to IP alignment scheme (10.100.<category>.<suffix>)

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **tofu/ip-registry.tf** - Central IP registry updated with traefik_ip convenience variable:
     ```hcl
     # Convenience: Traefik IP for route modules
     traefik_ip = local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik
     ```

   - **tofu/modules/docker-lxc/main.tf** and **variables.tf** - Updated for new network variables (container_ip, lan_ip)

   - **tofu/modules/lxc-base/main.tf** - Contains lifecycle ignore_changes block that prevents IP updates:
     ```hcl
     lifecycle {
       ignore_changes = [
         operating_system,
         initialization,  # Contains IP config - prevents API updates
         unprivileged,
         disk,
         features,
         tags,
         device_passthrough,
         console,
         start_on_boot,
         mount_point,
         # ... timeouts
       ]
     }
     ```

   - **tofu/apps/portainer/main.tf** - Example of single-NIC migration:
     ```hcl
     # Network (container network only - no LAN access needed)
     container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.core.portainer}${local.network.container_netmask}"
     ```

   - **tofu/apps/traefik/main.tf** - Example of dual-NIC migration:
     ```hcl
     # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for external access)
     container_ip = "${local.traefik_ip}${local.network.container_netmask}"
     lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.traefik}${local.network.lan_netmask}"
     ```

   - **tofu/apps/jellyfin/main.tf** - Added jellystat and requests routes:
     ```hcl
     module "jellystat_route" {
       source = "../../modules/traefik-route"
       app_name    = "jellystat"
       backend_url = "http://${module.jellyfin.ip_address}:3000"
       internal_domain = "jellystat.${var.domain_internal}"
       traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
       ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
       internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authelia", "internal-only"]
       depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
     }

     module "requests_route" {
       source = "../../modules/traefik-route"
       app_name    = "requests"
       backend_url = "http://${module.jellyfin.ip_address}:5055"
       internal_domain = "requests.${var.domain_internal}"
       public_domain   = "requests.${var.domain_public}"
       traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
       ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
       internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
       public_middlewares   = ["public-security"]
       depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
     }
     ```

   - **tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/** - Reduced to only essential centralized routes:
     - common.yml (shared middlewares)
     - traefik.yml (dashboard)
     - pve.yml (Proxmox VE)
     - pbs.yml (Proxmox Backup Server)

   - **tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/migrated-dynamic/** - 23 files moved here (excluded via exclude_patterns)

4. Errors and Fixes:
   - **filesync provider "inconsistent result" error**: When applying, the provider reported ID change from old IP to new IP as unexpected. User corrected me that this isn't a bug - changing host IP fundamentally changes the resource. Fix: Re-run plan/apply which creates new resources with correct IDs.
   
   - **Network not reachable after OpenTofu apply**: Container network changed but IP didn't update via API due to `initialization` in ignore_changes. Fix: Manually update via `pct set` then restart container.
   
   - **Invalid ip_registry references**: `local.ip_registry.core.traefik` and `local.ip_registry.apps.*` didn't exist. Fix: Created `local.traefik_ip` convenience variable and fixed all category paths.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Solved**: Traefik route drift - moved duplicates to migrated-dynamic/
   - **Solved**: IP registry references - fixed all paths and added convenience variable
   - **Solved**: App network config - updated all apps to use container_ip/lan_ip
   - **Solved**: Container migration - manually migrated all containers via pct set
   - **In Progress**: OpenTofu apply for remaining apps to sync routes/state

6. All User Messages:
   - "as for phase 3, why dont we handle that from opentofu directly applying the plan?"
   - "whats the harm in removing `network_interface` from the ignore_changes block? we had originally put it in there since PI was managed by dhcp so ip changes caused unnecessary drift"
   - "yes" (confirming to proceed with applying portainer as test)
   - "i dont think filesync has a bug, changing IP usually means a different host."

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Apply OpenTofu for remaining apps: authelia, openwebui, n8n, media-management, network-services, jellyfin, immich
   - Verify all services accessible after migration

8. Current Work:
   Executing Phase 3 network migration via OpenTofu. All containers have been manually migrated via `pct set` commands to new IPs:
   - Single-NIC: 100, 201, 202, 402, 500, 501, 502
   - Dual-NIC: 200, 101, 401, 304
   
   Currently applying OpenTofu for each app to:
   1. Sync state with new IPs
   2. Update Traefik routes to use 10.100.x.x backend URLs
   
   Completed applies: portainer, dashboards, traefik, monitoring
   
   Last command was applying traefik which showed "No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration."

9. Optional Next Step:
   Continue applying OpenTofu for remaining apps. Based on user's request "as for phase 3, why dont we handle that from opentofu directly applying the plan?" and the pattern established:
   
   ```bash
   task tofu:plan APP=authelia && task tofu:apply APP=authelia
   task tofu:plan APP=openwebui && task tofu:apply APP=openwebui
   task tofu:plan APP=n8n && task tofu:apply APP=n8n
   task tofu:plan APP=media-management && task tofu:apply APP=media-management
   task tofu:plan APP=network-services && task tofu:apply APP=network-services
   task tofu:plan APP=jellyfin && task tofu:apply APP=jellyfin
   task tofu:plan APP=immich && task tofu:apply APP=immich
   ```

   Then verify all services are accessible via Traefik..

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Network Architecture:
#   - 192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0): Home LAN - FIOS router, external access
#   - 10.100.0.0/16  (vmbr1): Container network - internal services
#
# IP Scheme (Container ID aligned with IP):
#   - 10.100.1.x:  Core services (LXC 100-149)
#   - 10.100.2.x:  Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249)
#   - 10.100.3.x:  Media - Photos (LXC 300-349)
#   - 10.100.4.x:  Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449)
#   - 10.100.5.x:  Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549)
#
# Dual-NIC Services (need 192.168.1.x for LAN compatibility):
#   - Traefik: Reverse proxy for LAN clients
#   - AdGuard: DNS for LAN devices
#   - Jellyfin: DLNA/casting
#   - Immich: Mobile app sync
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    # Home LAN (vmbr0)
    lan_gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    lan_netmask = "/24"
    lan_prefix  = "192.168.1"

    # Container network (vmbr1)
    container_gateway = "10.100.0.1"
    container_netmask = "/16"
    container_prefix  = "10.100"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - Container Network (10.100.x.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pattern: 10.100.<category>.<container_id_suffix>
  # Example: LXC 304 -> 10.100.3.104 (category 3, suffix 04)

  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure (192.168.1.x only - not containers)
    infrastructure = {
      router  = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host (vmbr0)
      # Proxmox also has 10.100.0.1 on vmbr1 (gateway for containers)
    }

    # Core services (LXC 100-149) -> 10.100.1.x
    core = {
      portainer        = "10.100.1.100"  # LXC 100 - Container management
      network_services = "10.100.1.101"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Tailscale
      pbs              = "10.100.1.102"  # LXC 102 - Proxmox Backup Server
    }

    # Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249) -> 10.100.2.x
    dashboards = {
      traefik    = "10.100.2.200"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
      dashboards = "10.100.2.201"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia   = "10.100.2.202"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
    }

    # Media - Photos (LXC 300-349) -> 10.100.3.x
    photos = {
      immich_importer = "10.100.3.103"  # LXC 303 - Photo import
      immich          = "10.100.3.104"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
    }

    # Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449) -> 10.100.4.x
    media = {
      jellyfin         = "10.100.4.101"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "10.100.4.102"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack
    }

    # Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549) -> 10.100.5.x
    monitoring = {
      monitoring = "10.100.5.100"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui  = "10.100.5.101"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n        = "10.100.5.102"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # LAN IPs for Dual-NIC Services (192.168.1.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # These services need direct LAN access for compatibility with home devices

  lan_ips = {
    traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - LAN clients access services
    network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - DNS for LAN devices
    jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - DLNA/casting
    immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Mobile app sync
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    # Core (100-149)
    100 = local.ip_registry.core.portainer
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    102 = local.ip_registry.core.pbs

    # Dashboards & Auth (200-249)
    200 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.authelia

    # Photos (300-349)
    303 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich

    # Media (400-449)
    401 = local.ip_registry.media.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.media.media_management

    # Monitoring & AI (500-549)
    500 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.dashboards,
      local.ip_registry.photos,
      local.ip_registry.media,
      local.ip_registry.monitoring,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  }

  lan_ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in local.lan_ips : name => "${ip}${local.network.lan_netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Convenience: Traefik IP for route modules
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Used by traefik-route modules to sync config to Traefik LXC
  traefik_ip = local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for validation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_container_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.dashboards),
    values(local.ip_registry.photos),
    values(local.ip_registry.media),
    values(local.ip_registry.monitoring),
  )

  _all_lan_ips = values(local.lan_ips)
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "container_ips" {
  description = "All container IPs (10.100.x.x)"
  value       = local._all_container_ips
}

output "lan_ips" {
  description = "LAN IPs for dual-NIC services (192.168.1.x)"
  value       = local.lan_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

output "network" {
  description = "Network configuration"
  value       = local.network
}

@startuml homelab-network-architecture
!theme plain
title Homelab Network & Service Architecture

' ============================================================================
' Style Configuration
' ============================================================================
skinparam {
    BackgroundColor white
    ComponentStyle rectangle
    PackageStyle frame
    DefaultFontName Monospace
    DefaultFontSize 11
    NoteFontSize 10
    ArrowColor #666666
    ComponentBorderColor #333333
    PackageBorderColor #555555
    DatabaseBorderColor #555555
    CloudBorderColor #555555
}

' Colors by category
!$CORE_COLOR = "#E8F5E9"
!$DASHBOARD_COLOR = "#E3F2FD"
!$PHOTOS_COLOR = "#FFF3E0"
!$MEDIA_COLOR = "#FCE4EC"
!$MONITORING_COLOR = "#F3E5F5"
!$INFRA_COLOR = "#ECEFF1"

' ============================================================================
' External Networks
' ============================================================================
cloud "Internet" as internet {
    [Cloudflare Tunnel] as cf_tunnel
    note right of cf_tunnel : Public domains\n*.rambtech.dev
}

' ============================================================================
' Home LAN (192.168.1.0/24 - vmbr0)
' ============================================================================
package "Home LAN\n192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0)" as lan #FFFDE7 {
    node "FIOS Router\n192.168.1.1" as router

    rectangle "LAN Clients" as lan_clients {
        [Desktop/Laptop]
        [Mobile Devices]
        [Smart TVs]
    }
}

' ============================================================================
' Proxmox Host
' ============================================================================
node "Proxmox VE (homelab)\n192.168.1.215 (vmbr0)\n10.100.0.1 (vmbr1)" as proxmox #ECEFF1 {

    ' ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ' Container Network (10.100.0.0/16 - vmbr1)
    ' ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    package "Container Network\n10.100.0.0/16 (vmbr1)" as container_net {

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Core Services (100-149) -> 10.100.1.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Core Services (10.100.1.x)" as core $CORE_COLOR {
            component "LXC 100: Portainer\n10.100.1.100" as portainer {
                [Portainer UI :9000]
                [Portainer Agent :9001]
            }

            component "LXC 101: Network Services\n10.100.1.101\nLAN: 192.168.1.196" as network_svc {
                [AdGuard Home :80/:53]
                [Tailscale Exit Node]
            }

            component "LXC 102: PBS\n10.100.1.102" as pbs {
                [Proxmox Backup :8007]
            }
        }

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Dashboards & Auth (200-249) -> 10.100.2.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Dashboards & Auth (10.100.2.x)" as dashboards $DASHBOARD_COLOR {
            component "LXC 200: Traefik\n10.100.2.200\nLAN: 192.168.1.235" as traefik {
                [Traefik :443 (websecure)]
                [Traefik :80 (web/tunnel)]
                [Dashboard :8080]
            }

            component "LXC 201: Dashboards\n10.100.2.201" as dashboard_apps {
                [Homepage :3000]
                [Dashy :4001]
                [Glances :61208]
            }

            component "LXC 202: Authelia\n10.100.2.202" as authelia {
                [Authelia :9091]
                [Redis :6379]
            }
        }

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Photos (300-349) -> 10.100.3.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Photos (10.100.3.x)" as photos $PHOTOS_COLOR {
            component "LXC 303: Immich Importer\n10.100.3.103" as importer {
                [Photo Import Scripts]
            }

            component "LXC 304: Immich\n10.100.3.104\nLAN: 192.168.1.222" as immich {
                [Immich Server :2283]
                [Machine Learning :3003]
                [PostgreSQL :5432]
                [Redis :6379]
            }
        }

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Media - Streaming (400-449) -> 10.100.4.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Media Streaming (10.100.4.x)" as media $MEDIA_COLOR {
            component "LXC 401: Jellyfin\n10.100.4.101\nLAN: 192.168.1.226" as jellyfin {
                [Jellyfin :8096]
                [Jellystat :3000]
                [Jellyseerr :5055]
            }

            component "LXC 402: Media Management\n10.100.4.102" as arr_stack {
                [Sonarr :8989]
                [Radarr :7878]
                [Lidarr :8686]
                [Prowlarr :9696]
                [Bazarr :6767]
                [qBittorrent :8080]
                [SABnzbd :8085]
            }
        }

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Monitoring & AI (500-549) -> 10.100.5.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Monitoring & AI (10.100.5.x)" as monitoring $MONITORING_COLOR {
            component "LXC 500: Monitoring\n10.100.5.100" as mon_stack {
                [Prometheus :9090]
                [Grafana :3000]
                [Alertmanager :9093]
                [Uptime Kuma :3001]
                [ntfy :8080]
                [OTEL Collector :4317/:4318]
            }

            component "LXC 501: OpenWebUI\n10.100.5.101" as openwebui {
                [OpenWebUI :3000]
                [Ollama :11434]
            }

            component "LXC 502: n8n\n10.100.5.102" as n8n {
                [n8n :5678]
            }
        }
    }

    ' ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ' Storage
    ' ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    database "ZFS Storage" as storage {
        [tank/data/library]
        [tank/backups]
        [nvme-containers]
    }
}

' ============================================================================
' Traffic Flow Connections
' ============================================================================

' Internet -> Cloudflare -> Traefik
internet --> cf_tunnel
cf_tunnel --> traefik : "Public traffic\n(web entrypoint :80)"

' LAN -> Router -> Traefik (via LAN IP)
router --> traefik : "LAN traffic\n192.168.1.235:443"
lan_clients --> router

' DNS Resolution
lan_clients ..> network_svc : "DNS queries\n192.168.1.196:53"

' Traefik reverse proxy to services
traefik --> dashboard_apps : "homepage/dashy"
traefik --> authelia : "auth forwarding"
traefik --> jellyfin : "jellyfin/requests"
traefik --> immich : "photos"
traefik --> mon_stack : "grafana/prometheus"
traefik --> openwebui : "ai"
traefik --> n8n : "n8n"
traefik --> arr_stack : "sonarr/radarr/etc"
traefik --> portainer : "portainer"
traefik --> pbs : "pbs"

' Authelia protects services
authelia ..> dashboard_apps : "ForwardAuth"
authelia ..> mon_stack : "ForwardAuth"

' Media flow
arr_stack --> jellyfin : "Media files"
jellyfin --> storage : "/data/library"
immich --> storage : "Photo storage"
pbs --> storage : "Backups"

' Monitoring
mon_stack ..> proxmox : "OTLP metrics"
mon_stack ..> portainer : "Scrape metrics"

' DLNA/Casting (via LAN IP)
lan_clients ..> jellyfin : "DLNA\n192.168.1.226"
lan_clients ..> immich : "Mobile sync\n192.168.1.222"

' ============================================================================
' Legend
' ============================================================================
legend bottom right
|= Network |= Range |= Purpose |
| vmbr0 | 192.168.1.0/24 | Home LAN |
| vmbr1 | 10.100.0.0/16 | Container network |
|= IP Scheme |= LXC Range |= Category |
| 10.100.1.x | 100-149 | Core services |
| 10.100.2.x | 200-249 | Dashboards & Auth |
| 10.100.3.x | 300-349 | Photos |
| 10.100.4.x | 400-449 | Media Streaming |
| 10.100.5.x | 500-549 | Monitoring & AI |
endlegend

@enduml

' ============================================================================
' Participants

box "External" #FFE0B2
    actor "Public User" as pub_user
    participant "Cloudflare\nTunnel" as cloudflare
end box

box "Home LAN (192.168.1.x)" #FFFDE7
    actor "LAN Client" as lan_user
    participant "AdGuard DNS\n192.168.1.196" as adguard
    participant "FIOS Router\n192.168.1.1" as router
end box

box "Container Network (10.100.x.x)" #E3F2FD
    participant "Traefik\n10.100.2.200\n(LAN: 192.168.1.235)" as traefik
    participant "Authelia\n10.100.2.202" as authelia
    participant "Backend Service\n(e.g., Grafana)" as backend
end box

' ============================================================================
' Public Access Flow
' ============================================================================
== Public Access (*.rambtech.dev) ==

pub_user -> cloudflare : HTTPS request\njellyfin.rambtech.dev
cloudflare -> traefik : HTTP :80\n(web entrypoint)
traefik -> backend : Proxy to backend\n10.100.x.x:port
backend --> traefik : Response
traefik --> cloudflare : Response
cloudflare --> pub_user : HTTPS response

note over cloudflare, traefik
Cloudflare tunnel terminates TLS
Traffic arrives at Traefik's 'web' entrypoint (HTTP)
end note

' ============================================================================
' Internal Access Flow (with Authelia)
' ============================================================================
== Internal Access with SSO (*.homelab.rambtech.dev) ==

lan_user -> adguard : DNS query\ngrafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
adguard --> lan_user : 192.168.1.235 (Traefik LAN IP)

lan_user -> traefik : HTTPS :443\ngrafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
traefik -> authelia : ForwardAuth check
authelia --> traefik : 401 Unauthorized

traefik --> lan_user : Redirect to auth.homelab.rambtech.dev
lan_user -> traefik : HTTPS to auth subdomain
traefik -> authelia : Load login page
authelia --> traefik : Login page
traefik --> lan_user : Show login page

lan_user -> traefik : Submit credentials
traefik -> authelia : Verify credentials
authelia --> traefik : Set session cookie + redirect
traefik --> lan_user : Redirect to original URL with cookie

lan_user -> traefik : HTTPS with session cookie
traefik -> authelia : ForwardAuth check
authelia --> traefik : 200 OK (valid session)
traefik -> backend : Proxy to grafana\n10.100.5.100:3000
backend --> traefik : Response
traefik --> lan_user : HTTPS response

note over traefik, authelia
Services protected by 'authelia' middleware
require ForwardAuth validation
end note

' ============================================================================
' Direct LAN Access Flow (DLNA/Mobile)
' ============================================================================
== Direct LAN Access (DLNA/Mobile Apps) ==

lan_user -> adguard : DNS query\njellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev
adguard --> lan_user : 192.168.1.235 (Traefik)

note over lan_user
But for DLNA/casting, apps use direct LAN IP
end note

lan_user -> "Jellyfin\n192.168.1.226" as jellyfin_lan : DLNA discovery\nor direct HTTP :8096
jellyfin_lan --> lan_user : Media stream

note over jellyfin_lan
Dual-NIC services have LAN IPs for:
- DLNA/Chromecast (Jellyfin)
- Mobile app sync (Immich)
- DNS queries (AdGuard)
end note

@enduml

content.text: Now let me update the ARCHITECTURE.md file to reference these diagrams:

content.content:
1→# Homelab OpenTofu Architecture
     2→
     3→Modern, self-contained app deployment pattern with zero symlinks and self-service routing.
     4→
     5→## Module Ecosystem
     6→
     7→### Core Modules
     8→
     9→| Module | Purpose | Replaces |
    10→|--------|---------|----------|
    11→| **common** | Shared resources (1Password, IP registry, variables) | 44 symlinked files |
    12→| **docker-lxc** | Complete Docker app deployment (LXC + Docker + files) | Manual LXC + provisioners |
    13→| **traefik-route** | Self-service Traefik route registration | Manual YAML editing |
    14→| **cloudflare-tunnel** | Self-service public DNS registration | Manual Cloudflare dashboard |
    15→
    16→### Supporting Modules
    17→
    18→| Module | Purpose |
    19→|--------|---------|
    20→| **lxc-base** | Base LXC container with static IP |
    21→| **file-sync** | Rsync file transfers to remote hosts |
    22→| **proxmox-notes** | Update LXC description in Proxmox UI |
    23→
    24→## The Golden Pattern
    25→
    26→A complete, self-contained app deployment:
    27→
    28→```hcl
    29→# 1. Shared resources (no symlinks!)
    30→module "common" {
    31→  source = "../../modules/common"
    32→}
    33→
    34→# 2. Deploy app LXC with Docker
    35→module "myapp" {
    36→  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"
    37→
    38→  name         = "myapp"
    39→  container_id = 150
    40→
    41→  ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
    42→  gateway    = module.common.network.gateway
    43→
    44→  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"
    45→
    46→  ssh_private_key_path = module.common.ssh_private_key_path
    47→  ssh_public_key       = module.common.ssh_public_key
    48→  template             = module.common.lxc_template_docker
    49→
    50→  # ... other config
    51→}
    52→
    53→# 3. Self-register Traefik routes
    54→module "myapp_route" {
    55→  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"
    56→
    57→  app_name    = "myapp"
    58→  backend_url = "http://${module.myapp.ip_address}:8080"
    59→
    60→  internal_domain = "myapp.${module.common.domain_internal}"
    61→  public_domain   = "myapp.${module.common.domain_public}"  # Optional
    62→
    63→  traefik_host         = "192.168.1.162"
    64→  ssh_private_key_path = module.common.ssh_private_key_path
    65→
    66→  depends_on = [module.myapp]
    67→}
    68→
    69→# 4. Self-register public DNS (optional)
    70→module "myapp_tunnel" {
    71→  source = "../../modules/cloudflare-tunnel"
    72→
    73→  hostname    = "myapp"
    74→  domain      = module.common.domain_public
    75→  backend_url = "http://192.168.1.162"  # Traefik
    76→  tunnel_id   = module.common.op.cloudflare_tunnel_id
    77→
    78→  depends_on = [module.myapp_route]
    79→}
    80→```
    81→
    82→## What This Achieves
    83→
    84→### ✅ Self-Contained Apps
    85→
    86→Each app directory contains **everything** needed:
    87→- `main.tf` - Complete app definition
    88→- `deploy/` - Docker compose + configs
    89→
    90→No symlinks, no manual Traefik edits, no Cloudflare dashboard.
    91→
    92→### ✅ Declarative Networking
    93→
    94→```hcl
    95→# App says "I want to be accessible at these URLs"
    96→internal_domain = "myapp.homelab.rambtech.dev"
    97→public_domain   = "myapp.rambtech.dev"
    98→
    99→# Infrastructure automatically:
   100→# 1. Creates Traefik routes
   101→# 2. Syncs configs to Traefik LXC
   102→# 3. Reloads Traefik
   103→# 4. Creates Cloudflare DNS
   104→# 5. Updates Proxmox notes
   105→```
   106→
   107→### ✅ Single Source of Truth
   108→

# Homelab OpenTofu Architecture

Modern, self-contained app deployment pattern with zero symlinks and self-service routing.

## Module Ecosystem

### Core Modules

| Module | Purpose | Replaces |
|--------|---------|----------|
| **common** | Shared resources (1Password, IP registry, variables) | 44 symlinked files |
| **docker-lxc** | Complete Docker app deployment (LXC + Docker + files) | Manual LXC + provisioners |
| **traefik-route** | Self-service Traefik route registration | Manual YAML editing |
| **cloudflare-tunnel** | Self-service public DNS registration | Manual Cloudflare dashboard |

### Supporting Modules

| Module | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| **lxc-base** | Base LXC container with static IP |
| **file-sync** | Rsync file transfers to remote hosts |
| **proxmox-notes** | Update LXC description in Proxmox UI |

## The Golden Pattern

A complete, self-contained app deployment:

```hcl
# 1. Shared resources (no symlinks!)
module "common" {
  source = "../../modules/common"
}

# 2. Deploy app LXC with Docker
module "myapp" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "myapp"
  container_id = 150

  ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
  gateway    = module.common.network.gateway

  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"

  ssh_private_key_path = module.common.ssh_private_key_path
  ssh_public_key       = module.common.ssh_public_key
  template             = module.common.lxc_template_docker

  # ... other config
}

# 3. Self-register Traefik routes
module "myapp_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "myapp"
  backend_url = "http://${module.myapp.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "myapp.${module.common.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "myapp.${module.common.domain_public}"  # Optional

  traefik_host         = "192.168.1.162"
  ssh_private_key_path = module.common.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [module.myapp]
}

# 4. Self-register public DNS (optional)
module "myapp_tunnel" {
  source = "../../modules/cloudflare-tunnel"

  hostname    = "myapp"
  domain      = module.common.domain_public
  backend_url = "http://192.168.1.162"  # Traefik
  tunnel_id   = module.common.op.cloudflare_tunnel_id

  depends_on = [module.myapp_route]
}
```

## What This Achieves

### ✅ Self-Contained Apps

Each app directory contains **everything** needed:
- `main.tf` - Complete app definition
- `deploy/` - Docker compose + configs

No symlinks, no manual Traefik edits, no Cloudflare dashboard.

### ✅ Declarative Networking

```hcl
# App says "I want to be accessible at these URLs"
internal_domain = "myapp.homelab.rambtech.dev"
public_domain   = "myapp.rambtech.dev"

# Infrastructure automatically:
# 1. Creates Traefik routes
# 2. Syncs configs to Traefik LXC
# 3. Reloads Traefik
# 4. Creates Cloudflare DNS
# 5. Updates Proxmox notes
```

### ✅ Single Source of Truth

- **IP registry** in common module
- **Secrets** from 1Password via common module
- **Routes** defined in app, not scattered across Traefik configs
- **DNS** defined in app, not Cloudflare dashboard

### ✅ Clean Directory Structure

**Before (with symlinks):**
```
tofu/apps/myapp/
├── main.tf
├── deploy/
├── shared.tf -> ../../shared.tf
├── onepassword.tf -> ../../onepassword.tf
├── ip-registry.tf -> ../../ip-registry.tf
└── versions.tf -> ../../versions.tf
```

**After (with common module):**
```
tofu/apps/myapp/
├── main.tf       # Just one file!
└── deploy/
```

## Traffic Flow

### Internal Access (HTTPS)

```
User Browser
   ↓
https://myapp.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ↓
Traefik (192.168.1.162)
   ↓ Let's Encrypt TLS
http://192.168.1.150:8080  # App LXC
```

### Public Access (HTTPS)

```
Internet User
   ↓
https://myapp.rambtech.dev
   ↓
Cloudflare Edge (TLS termination)
   ↓
Cloudflare Tunnel
   ↓
Traefik (192.168.1.162) - HTTP
   ↓
http://192.168.1.150:8080  # App LXC
```

## Deployment Workflow

### New App Deployment

```bash
# 1. Get next available IP
task ip:next
# Output: 192.168.1.150

# 2. Create app directory
mkdir -p tofu/apps/myapp/deploy

# 3. Write main.tf using golden pattern

# 4. Write docker-compose.yml in deploy/

# 5. Update IP registry in common module
# tofu/modules/common/main.tf:
#   myapp = "192.168.1.150"

# 6. Deploy
task tofu:init APP=myapp
task tofu:plan APP=myapp
task tofu:apply APP=myapp

# Done! App is:
# - Running in LXC
# - Accessible at myapp.homelab.rambtech.dev
# - Optionally public at myapp.rambtech.dev
# - Documented in Proxmox notes
```

### Update App Configuration

```bash
# 1. Edit deploy/docker-compose.yml or other files
vim tofu/apps/myapp/deploy/docker-compose.yml

# 2. Apply changes
task tofu:apply APP=myapp

# file-sync module auto-syncs changed files
# remote-docker-compose provider auto-restarts containers
```

### Change Routes

```hcl
# Edit main.tf
module "myapp_route" {
  # ...
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "rate-limit"]  # Added
}

# Apply
task tofu:apply APP=myapp

# Traefik config auto-updated and reloaded
```

## Migration Path

### Phase 1: Create Core Modules ✅

- [x] common module (replaces symlinks)
- [x] docker-lxc module (gold standard)
- [x] traefik-route module (self-service routing)
- [x] cloudflare-tunnel module (self-service DNS)

### Phase 2: Migrate One App (n8n)

1. Update n8n/main.tf to use common module
2. Add traefik-route module
3. Add cloudflare-tunnel module (if public)
4. Test thoroughly
5. Remove symlinks

### Phase 3: Migrate Remaining Apps

Use n8n as template for:
- authelia
- dashboards
- immich
- immich-importer
- jellyfin
- media-management
- monitoring
- openwebui
- portainer

### Phase 4: Migrate Traefik (Complex)

Traefik is special (doesn't run Docker currently):
- Use lxc-base + file-sync modules
- Keep existing manual setup initially
- Gradually adopt new patterns

### Phase 5: Cleanup

1. Delete `tofu/shared.tf`
2. Delete `tofu/onepassword.tf`
3. Delete `tofu/ip-registry.tf`
4. Delete `tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/*.yml` (now auto-generated)
5. Update CLAUDE.md documentation

## Benefits Summary

### Code Reduction

- **44 symlinks** → 0 symlinks
- **186 lines** per app → **96 lines** per app (48% reduction)
- **Manual Traefik configs** → Auto-generated from app definition
- **Manual Cloudflare DNS** → Auto-created from app definition

### Developer Experience

- **One file** to understand app deployment
- **No context switching** between Traefik/Cloudflare/app
- **Clear dependencies** via module structure
- **Self-documenting** architecture

### Operational Excellence

- **Single source of truth** for all app config
- **Atomic updates** via Terraform state
- **Rollback friendly** (destroy and recreate)
- **Testable** (each module independently testable)

## Best Practices

### 1. Always Use Common Module

```hcl
module "common" {
  source = "../../modules/common"
}
```

Never hardcode values that common module provides.

### 2. Use docker-lxc for Docker Apps

Don't use lxc-base + manual Docker setup. The docker-lxc module is the gold standard.

### 3. Self-Register Routes

Every app should include its traefik-route module. Don't manually edit Traefik configs.

### 4. Declare Public Access Explicitly

```hcl
# Clear intent: this app is public
public_domain = "myapp.rambtech.dev"

module "myapp_tunnel" { ... }
```

### 5. Document Custom Notes

Use `custom_notes` in docker-lxc for app-specific instructions:

```hcl
custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Special Configuration

This app requires manual SSL cert installation:
```
ssh root@${module.myapp.ip_address}
# ... steps
```
EOT
```

## Future Enhancements

- **Auto-discovery** of app changes (watch docker-compose.yml)
- **Multi-backend** Traefik routes (load balancing)
- **Auto-scaling** based on metrics
- **Backup automation** via module
- **Testing framework** for modules
- **VS Code snippets** for golden pattern

# Traefik config auto-updated and reloaded
```

## Migration Path

### Phase 1: Create Core Modules ✅

- [x] common module (replaces symlinks)
- [x] docker-lxc module (gold standard)
- [x] traefik-route module (self-service routing)
- [x] cloudflare-tunnel module (self-service DNS)

### Phase 2: Migrate One App (n8n)

1. Update n8n/main.tf to use common module
2. Add traefik-route module
3. Add cloudflare-tunnel module (if public)
4. Test thoroughly
5. Remove symlinks

### Phase 3: Migrate Remaining Apps

Use n8n as template for:
- authelia
- dashboards
- immich
- immich-importer
- jellyfin
- media-management
- monitoring
- openwebui
- portainer

### Phase 4: Migrate Traefik (Complex)

Traefik is special (doesn't run Docker currently):
- Use lxc-base + file-sync modules
- Keep existing manual setup initially
- Gradually adopt new patterns

### Phase 5: Cleanup

1. Delete `tofu/shared.tf`
2. Delete `tofu/onepassword.tf`
3. Delete `tofu/ip-registry.tf`
4. Delete `tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/*.yml` (now auto-generated)
5. Update CLAUDE.md documentation

## Benefits Summary

### Code Reduction

- **44 symlinks** → 0 symlinks
- **186 lines** per app → **96 lines** per app (48% reduction)
- **Manual Traefik configs** → Auto-generated from app definition
- **Manual Cloudflare DNS** → Auto-created from app definition

### Developer Experience

- **One file** to understand app deployment
- **No context switching** between Traefik/Cloudflare/app
- **Clear dependencies** via module structure
- **Self-documenting** architecture

### Operational Excellence

- **Single source of truth** for all app config
- **Atomic updates** via Terraform state
- **Rollback friendly** (destroy and recreate)
- **Testable** (each module independently testable)

## Best Practices

### 1. Always Use Common Module

```hcl
module "common" {
  source = "../../modules/common"
}
```

Never hardcode values that common module provides.

### 2. Use docker-lxc for Docker Apps

Don't use lxc-base + manual Docker setup. The docker-lxc module is the gold standard.

### 3. Self-Register Routes

Every app should include its traefik-route module. Don't manually edit Traefik configs.

### 4. Declare Public Access Explicitly

```hcl
# Clear intent: this app is public
public_domain = "myapp.rambtech.dev"

module "myapp_tunnel" { ... }
```

### 5. Document Custom Notes

Use `custom_notes` in docker-lxc for app-specific instructions:

```hcl
custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Special Configuration

This app requires manual SSL cert installation:
```
ssh root@${module.myapp.ip_address}
# ... steps
```
EOT
```

## Future Enhancements

- **Auto-discovery** of app changes (watch docker-compose.yml)
- **Multi-backend** Traefik routes (load balancing)
- **Auto-scaling** based on metrics
- **Backup automation** via module
- **Testing framework** for modules
- **VS Code snippets** for golden pattern
